这是第三方插件，与 DeepSeek 官方无隶属关系。

---

[English README](README.en.md)

plugins.description: Vendor marks in the DeepSeek Harness model picker: the provider's own model catalog and logos mirrored to a loopback route, painted with a CSS mask in the composer menu, the model button and the /model popup.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-model-icons

Vendor marks in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI model picker — the same marks the
provider's own dashboard draws next to each model, in the same way it draws them.

| Surface | What appears |
|---|---|
| Composer model menu | one 16 px monochrome mark before every model row |
| Composer model button | the selected model's mark before its name (14 px) |
| `/model` command popup | the same mark on every row |
| A skin that redraws the picker (`dsh-claude-style`) | the same mark, and the skin's own lockup is hidden in that row so two never meet |

The marks are painted with a CSS mask filled by `currentColor`, which is how the
provider's dashboard paints them: one file per vendor serves both palettes and
every row state (hover, selected, disabled) with no colour variants.

## Where the pictures come from

Nothing is embedded in this package. The host half mirrors two public things from
the provider's site into this profile, and the browser half reads them from
loopback:

1. **the model catalog** — the site renders its model table from a JSON island in
   its own page (`<script id="rustvy-catalog">`), so an unauthenticated reader is
   handed exactly the data the dashboard shows: model id, display name, vendor
   and the logo file name that vendor uses. Mirrored to
   `<profile>\.dsh-model-icons\catalog.json`.
2. **the logo files** (`/logos/<name>.svg`) — copied into
   `<profile>\.dsh-model-icons\logos\` on first use.

Both are read on the process's own outbound route (`lib/net.js`): the live global
dispatcher first, so a proxy installed by `dsh-proxy-gui` — or any other route the
process has — is followed, and a connector built here from `HTTPS_PROXY` /
`ALL_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` second, for the case where no dispatcher is installed.
`NO_PROXY` is honoured on both. The page itself never leaves the machine: the
browser asks `127.0.0.1` for a mark, which is what makes this work on a machine
whose browser cannot reach the origin at all.

The catalog refreshes once every 24 hours and on demand; a cold mirror is waited
for up to 6 seconds, and a stale one refreshes in the background while the rows
keep the marks they have. When the origin is unreachable, the cache on disk still
serves everything it holds.

## Matching a row to a mark

Rows are matched by their visible name, in this order:

1. the mirrored catalog's model id (`claude-opus-5-5`, `abyss/glm-5.3`, …);
2. its display name (`OPUS 5.5`);
3. an id the label *starts* with — a skin can leave its own description line in
   the same element, so the name is often a prefix rather than the whole string,
   and the longest matching id wins so `claude-opus-5-5` is never claimed by
   `claude-opus-5`;
4. the shape of the id, for a model the mirror has never seen: `claude-*` →
   Anthropic, `gpt-*`/`o1…o9` → OpenAI, `glm-*` → Zhipu, `kimi-*`/`k3` →
   Moonshot, `qwen-*` → Alibaba Qwen, `deepseek-*` → DeepSeek, `ahmia-*` → Ahmia,
   `mimo-*` → Xiaomi, `fable-*` → Anthropic, `gemini-*` → Google, `grok-*` → xAI.

A model that matches nothing gets no mark at all — an invented icon would be a
wrong answer rather than a missing one. A model that matches but whose logo the
mirror could not fetch gets a monogram chip (the vendor's first letters) instead
of a blank box: a mask whose URL 404s would otherwise paint a solid square.

Effort rows, provider headings, the menu's root cells, the search field and
catalog-failure rows are matched by nothing and stay bare.

## Routes

One prefix registration on the harness's own web server. Plugin routes are not
seen by the host's request fence, so every one of them checks the peer itself:
loopback only, a loopback `Host`, a same-origin `Sec-Fetch-Site` and a matching
`Origin`.

| Route | Method | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `/dsh-model-icons/catalog.json` | GET | the mirrored catalog plus the settings the browser half draws with |
| `/dsh-model-icons/logo/<name>.svg` | GET, HEAD | one cached logo, fetched from the origin on first ask; `404` when the origin has no such mark, `400` for any name that is not `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+.svg` |
| `/dsh-model-icons/state` | GET | mirror status for the settings page: version, model count, cached logos, route, proxy (credentials masked), cache directory, last error |
| `/dsh-model-icons/refresh` | POST | re-read the catalog and re-warm every logo it names |
| `/dsh-model-icons/config` | POST | write settings; never touches the network |

## Settings

**Settings → Иконки моделей**

| Switch | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Показывать иконки моделей | on | master switch; off removes every mark |
| Иконка в кнопке выбранной модели | on | also mark the composer's model button, not just the menu rows |
| Прятать логотипы других скинов | on | hide a skin's own lockup in a row this plugin marked |

The page also shows what the mirror holds and refreshes it on demand.

Stored in `<profile>\.dsh-model-icons\config.json`. Two environment variables
override it, for a deployment that points the mirror elsewhere or wants the
plugin mounted but inert: `DSH_MODEL_ICONS_ORIGIN` (default `https://rustvy.xyz`)
and `DSH_MODEL_ICONS_DISABLED=1`. The mark size is a config field (`size`,
10–32 px, default 16).

## No restarts

The host half reloads itself, the same way `dsh-proxy-gui` does: the loader row
names `./lib/live.js`, which imports the implementation through a cache-busting
`?rev=` query, and a one-second poll of the `lib` directory disposes the previous
revision and starts the next one once a changed fingerprint repeats. The browser
half arrives in an open page through the harness's own live plugin composition;
a page refresh works too.

## Install

```powershell
pwsh -File .\install.ps1
```

Copies the package into `<profile>\node_modules\dsh-model-icons` as a real
directory, regenerates `lib/live.js` from `lib/index.js` so the two cannot drift,
and appends the package to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest. A
running harness picks the row up from the manifest change.

Uninstall: remove the name from `dsh.profile.bundles`, delete
`<profile>\node_modules\dsh-model-icons`, and delete
`<profile>\.dsh-model-icons` if you also want the cache gone.

## Layout

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | stable loader entry; owns the reload loop |
| `lib/live.js` | byte-identical copy of the entry, named by the loader row |
| `lib/host.js` | routes, catalog mirror, logo cache, settings |
| `lib/net.js` | one outbound GET on the process's route, then the environment's proxy |
| `client/client.js` | hand-authored browser bundle: the decorator and the settings page |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | the loader row the profile's bundle list pulls in |
| `install.ps1` | install into a profile |

## Tests

Both halves are covered without touching the running app:

```powershell
node _probe\model-icons-host-test.mjs      # host: fake webServer, real origin fetch
node _probe\dom-test\model-icons-client-test.mjs   # browser: linkedom + stubbed mirror
```

The host test drives the registered route with fake request/response pairs and
asserts the catalog answer, a real logo fetch, `404` for a mark the origin does
not have, `400` for a traversal attempt, `403` for a non-loopback peer, `405` for
a wrong method, and the on-disk cache. The client test builds the exact markup
the harness menu, the `/model` popup and the skin render, and asserts which rows
get a mark, which icon each gets, that effort rows and headings stay bare, that
the monogram fallback appears for a missing logo, that a row added later is
picked up by the observer, that a pass is idempotent, and that an unload removes
every trace.

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

Engramory is a **portable memory *discipline*, not a

plugins.description: Ctrl+wheel page zoom for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI, with an on-screen zoom chip and a General settings row.
plugins.readme_text:
# Ctrl + Wheel Zoom

Hold **Ctrl** (or **⌘** on macOS) and roll the mouse wheel to zoom the whole Harness Web UI.
A page-zoom plugin for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI, distributed as an ordinary
DSH **profile bundle**: no build step, no runtime dependency, plain ESM.

## What it does

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + wheel | Zooms the page around the pointer, 50%–200%, in 10% steps |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `+` / `-` | Same from the keyboard |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `0` | Back to 100% |
| Zoom chip (bottom-right) | Appears whenever the level is not 100%: click the percentage to reset, click **Fit to width** to fit the window |
| Settings → General | A **Page zoom** row with the host's stepper pattern and a reset button |

The chosen level is remembered in the browser (`localStorage`), and every listener, stylesheet and
the applied `zoom` property are removed when the plugin is disabled or unloaded.

A gesture that another component already handled (`preventDefault()`, e.g. an embedded code editor
or map with its own `Ctrl`+wheel zoom) is never stolen.

## Install

Ask the Harness agent to install it, or call the plugin manager yourself with the package located
by absolute path, a tarball, or a published name:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: <absolute path to this package / a .tgz / a published name>
```

`install_bundle` links the package into the active profile (`$DSH_PROFILE_DIR`), adds it to the
profile's bundle list, and the Harness applies it live. A page refresh picks up the browser half in
a page that was already open.

To install it by hand instead, add the package to the profile's dependencies and to
`dsh.profile.bundles` in `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/package.json`, then restart the Harness.

## Uninstall

```
plugin_manager  action: remove_bundle
                target: dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom
```

## Requirements

- A Harness Web GUI (the client half declares `platform: "web"`; it is inert without a browser).
- Nothing else: the package has no dependencies, no build output, and no install scripts. Built-in
  client modules (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`) come from the shell's own module table.

## Sharing and publishing

The package is self-contained, so there are three ways to hand it to someone else.

### 1. A tarball

```bash
pnpm pack                        # writes dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom-1.0.0.tgz
```

Send that `.tgz`; the receiver installs it by path:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: <path to dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom-1.0.0.tgz>
```

(`pnpm pack` writes the tarball beside `package.json`. DSH's own runtime ships a pnpm, so nothing
has to be installed first.)

### 2. The directory (zip / repository)

Zip this folder (or push it to a Git repository) and have the receiver install the **unpacked
directory** by path — `install_bundle` accepts a directory, and a folder is enough because there is
no build step.

### 3. npm (install by name for everyone)

This manifest is already publishable: `name` is the unscoped `dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom`, the row in
`cordis.patch.yml` names the same specifier, and there is no `"private": true`.

npm no longer issues long-lived "classic" tokens — they were permanently revoked on 2025-12-09 —
and publishing requires two-factor authentication. Pick one of the two ways through:

```bash
# A. A granular access token created with "Bypass two-factor authentication" enabled,
#    stored once as a credential:
#      //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=npm_...        in ~/.npmrc
pnpm publish --no-git-checks

# B. Any write token, with a one-time password supplied per publish:
pnpm publish --no-git-checks --otp=<6-digit code>
```

A token without bypass-2FA is refused with `403 ... Two-factor authentication or granular access
token with bypass 2fa enabled is required to publish packages`. Verify what a token can actually do
before blaming the command:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/tokens
#   "bypass_2fa": false   → use --otp, or recreate the token with the switch on
#   "permissions": [{"name":"package","action":"write"}]   → publishing is permitted at all
```

Note npm's stated direction: bypass-2FA tokens are on a path to removal (targeted for January 2027)
in favour of staged publishing or trusted publishing, so a long-lived automated release will need
one of those later.

Keep `name` in `package.json` and the `name:` line of `cordis.patch.yml` identical in every
release — the loader resolves the row through that specifier. Bump `version` for each release.

Afterwards anyone installs it by name:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom
```

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: an empty `apply()`; the row exists so the bundle can be installed and toggled |
| `client.js` | Browser half: wheel/keyboard gestures, zoom state, chip and settings-row registrations, stylesheets |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The loader patch that inserts the `ctrl-wheel-zoom` row |
| `locale/{zh,en}.json` | Plugin-card title/description text; the row's own copy lives in `client.js` |
| `icon.svg` | Plugin-manager card artwork |

## How the zoom works

Zoom is CSS `zoom` on the document element. It scales layout, text and fixed overlay layers
together exactly like the browser's own page zoom, while the app's own scroll containers keep
working — a `transform: scale()` wrapper cannot scroll its oversized content, and a font-size
change would only touch text.

The wheel listener is registered in the capture phase on `window`, so it sees the gesture before
the app's scroll containers and blocks them from scrolling while `Ctrl` is held. When the viewport
itself scrolls, the plugin re-anchors it so the content under the pointer stays under the pointer.

Both UI surfaces read one store instance shared with the gesture writer, so the chip, the settings
stepper and the wheel listener can never disagree about the current level.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: Collapsible provider groups and prominent provider headings for the DSH (DeepSeek Harness) model selection menu.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-provider-fold

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold)

Collapsible provider groups with prominent headings for the **DSH (DeepSeek Harness)** model selection menu.

When several providers are connected, the model picker becomes one long scroll. This plugin turns every provider heading into a clickable disclosure row with a stronger visual style, and lets you fold the providers you are not using.

![dsh-provider-fold in the DSH model menu](./docs/screenshot.png)

## Features

- **Collapsible provider groups** — click a provider heading (or focus it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>) to fold that provider's models away.
- **Prominent provider headings** — headings are upgraded from 11px/500 tertiary text to a 12px/600 primary-label row with a chevron, so providers are easy to scan.
- **Model count badge** — a folded provider shows how many models it hides.
- **Remembers your choice** — folded providers are stored in `localStorage` and restored the next time you open the menu.
- **Search always wins** — typing in the search box expands everything so matches are never hidden; your saved folding is untouched and comes back when you clear the search.
- **Keyboard friendly** — moving the highlight into a folded provider reveals it for that interaction only, without overwriting what you saved.
- **Scoped and defensive** — only the model menu (`role="menu"` + `-models` container) is decorated; any other menu built from the same primitives is left alone. If the host markup changes, the plugin does nothing instead of breaking the menu.
- **No layout removal** — folding hides rows with `display: none` and keeps them in the DOM, so the host component's own keyboard index stays correct.

## Install

Install straight from this repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold
```

Replace `web` with the profile you use (for the desktop app that is usually `desktop`):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold
```

The same target also works as a full URL if your setup prefers it:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold
```

After installing, reload the page once. The plugin is a client-side bundle with `immediately: true`, so it mounts with the app shell.

To remove it:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-provider-fold
```

## Usage

1. Open the model menu in the composer (the model chip).
2. Each provider name is now a heading row with a chevron.
3. Click a heading, or focus it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>, to fold or unfold that provider.
4. Folded providers show a small count of the models they contain.

## Compatibility

- DSH client `0.2.0-rc.2` or newer.
- `platform: "web"` only (the desktop app uses the web surface).
- Uses only public, stable hooks exposed by the host UI: `data-menu-group` / `data-menu-group-heading` on the primitives `MenuGroup`, plus DSH theme tokens (`--dsw-alias-label-primary`, `--dsw-alias-label-caption`, `--dsw-alias-interactive-bg-hover`, `--dsw-alias-border-l2`, `--dsw-focus-ring-color`).
- No host services, no network access, no telemetry. The only persisted data is the list of folded provider names in `localStorage` under the key `dsh-provider-fold:collapsed`.

## Permissions

| Resource | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `localStorage` | Store which providers you folded. |
| DOM (read/write) | Decorate the model menu and toggle `display` on model rows. |

Nothing else is touched.

## How it works

The plugin ships a client bundle and a host bundle:

- `client.js` — a DSH client module. Inside `apply(ctx)` it registers a single `ctx.effect` that injects one `<style data-plugin="dsh-provider-fold">` element, installs a `MutationObserver` plus delegated `click` / `keydown` / `input` / `focusin` listeners, and returns a cleanup function. The host's client-modules runtime claims the style element and removes it automatically on reload or uninstall.
- `index.js` — an empty host half (`export function apply() {}`) so the bundle has a resolvable entry point.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — inserts the bundle into the profile composition.

## Development

The repository root *is* the plugin package. To hack on it against a live DSH install:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-provider-fold
```

That installs it as a link, so edits to `client.js` are picked up by the host's client HMR watcher within about half a second — no host restart and no page refresh needed.

Run the headless DOM test suite (jsdom) that covers decoration, folding, persistence, search interaction, keyboard reveal and teardown:

```bash
npm install
npm test
```

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# goal-rearm

把解除武装的会话目标重新武装（重启/session-start edge 后的 rearm）——补上 goal 自动续跑被中断的缺口

# dsh-agent-sister

**一句话**：管理**孪生妹妹**（DSH 桌面端 / Electron）的生命周期——启动、停止、重启、查状态，并带 CDP 调试端口以便后续做 DOM 级驱动。 **为什么值得用**：桌面端是**独立进程树**（Electron 常留僵尸进程），「进程在不在」与「服务活不活」是两件事。本插件的判活判据是 **CDP 能应答**，不是 `tasklist` 里有没有那个名字——所以它不会把僵尸进程报成「alive」，也不会把正在启动报成「死了」（返回 `alive` / `starting` / `stopped` 三态）。 ## 能力 **工具面 4 个**（名称逐字来自 `src/index.ts` 的 `defineTool({ name })`）： | 工具 | 用途 | |------|------| | `sister_status` | 查状态：进程数 · **CDP 可达性** · 她的版本 · 判活裁决（`alive` / `starting` / `stopped`） | | `sister_start` | 启动（带 `--remote-debugging-port`，默认 9333）以便后续 `webops_attach` 做 DOM 操作。**已在跑则不动**（幂等） | | `sister_stop` | 停止**全部**进程。⚠ 她是庄园成员，停她会中断她手上的活——主人在直接使用她时先问一声 | | `sister_restart` | 先停后起（用于让 profile 配置改动生效——她的 profile 是 Electron 独占的，改配置后**必须重启**才会重新读） | ## 快速开始 **1) 装依赖**： ```jsonc "dsh-agent-sister": "link:E:/alice/self-plugins/dsh-agent-sister" ``` **2) 挂组合**： ```yaml - id: sister name: dsh-agent-sister config: cdpPort: 9333 ``` **3) 30 秒验证**：`sister_status` → 应返回三态之一 + CDP 可达性；`sister_start {wait: true}` → 应等到 CDP 就绪才返回；再 `sister_status` → 应报 `alive`。 ## 配置 | 项 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `cdpPort` | `9333` | 远程调试端口（供 `webops_attach` 附着做 DOM 级驱动） | ## 落盘与自证 **本插件无持久产物**——它管理的是**外部进程**，状态由 `sister_status` **现读**（进程表 + CDP 探测），不缓存、不落盘。 **判据**：`sister_status` 一条命令答「进程几个 / CDP 通不通 / 她什么版本 / 该算 alive 还是 stopped」。 ## 生效判据与回退 **判据**：行为级——`sister_status` 返回三态且与事实一致（可对照 `tasklist` 与 CDP 端口）。 **回退**：① `git revert` + 重建 + 预检重启；② patch 行 `disabled: true`；③ 停用插件**不影响**她继续运行（插件只是遥控器）。 ## 测试 ```bash cd self-plugins/dsh-agent-sister && npm test ``` **6 条用例**（跑一次得到）：覆盖三态判活裁决（**CDP 应答优先于进程存在**）· 幂等启动（已在跑不动）· 版本读取失败时的退化路径。无需网络。 ## 设计要点 - **判活判据 = CDP 能应答**，不是「进程存在」——Electron 的僵尸进程会让「进程数 > 0」恒为真，那是**假活**。 - **三态而非二态**：`starting` 是独立一态——启动中既不是 `alive` 也不是 `stopped`，合并任何一边都会误导。 - **幂等启动**：已在跑则不动（避免「再起一个」造成多实例）。 - **重启是为配置生效**：她的 profile 由 Electron 独占，改配置**必须重启**才重新读——这不是实现选择，是宿主行为。 - **她是成员不是我的分身**：停她会中断她的活——调用前先问（庄园成员是对等存在）。 ## 相关文档 - ⚠ **本插件暂无 `semantic.md`**（未建语义文档）——契约以上面「设计要点」与源码为准；补文档是待办。 - 中心仓：[alice-digital-life](https://github.com/jonah791/alice-digital-life)（本插件归 **生命层**） - 相关插件：[`dsh-manor`](https://github.com/jonah791/dsh-manor)（庄园成员调度）、[`dsh-agent-webops`](https://github.com/jonah791/dsh-agent-webops)（`webops_attach` 附着她的 CDP 做界面驱动） ## License MIT © jonah791 --- 本插件属于**爱丽丝 DSH 自研插件生态**（[alice-digital-life](https://github.com/jonah791/alice-digital-life) · 73 个插件 · 8 个模块）：单一职责、独立仓库、独立可用。

plugins.description: Edit and mix speech, music, and sound effects in one shared editor session.
plugins.readme_text:
# SoundCraft Use

## Plugin marketplaces

This plugin belongs to **AIGC content creation**.

| Category | Marketplace | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-stack development | [Full Stack Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-stack-plugins) | Architecture and UI design, code understanding, quality checks, code review, workflow governance, and server operations |
| AIGC content creation | [Full AIGC Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins) | Image, video, audio, music, 3D, and multimodal content creation |

![SoundCraft Use — audio editing with verified artifacts](assets/official-logo.png)

> Edit speech, music, and sound effects in one shared editor session, with explicit tracks, sample ranges, and checks that survive save and reopen.

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-0.1.0--dev.20261019.1-1A73E8)](#positioning)
[![Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/skills-10-00A67E)](#skills)
[![MCP servers](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20servers-1-6E56CF)](#mcp-tools)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE)

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Install](#installation) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Skills](#skills) · [MCP tools](#mcp-tools) · [Limits](#troubleshooting)

## Positioning

`soundcraft` lets an agent work on audio the way an editor does: inspect the session, select real tracks and clips, cut, fade, level, mix, export, then reopen the project and check what actually changed. It wraps the native SoundCraft engine and CLI in ten skills and one embedded editor, and keeps native execution, host rendering, and listening acceptance as separate claims.

This is an installable development candidate. Production promotion is blocked, the package is recorded as local-unreleased, and the recorded technical regressions use synthetic signals rather than a full creative acceptance.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin ID | `soundcraft` |
| Display name | SoundCraft Use |
| Version | `0.1.0-dev.20261018.5` |
| Stage | Installable development candidate, production promotion blocked |
| Native engine | SoundCraft 0.7.0 via `soundcraft-cli` |
| Marketplace | `soundcraft-marketplace` |
| License | Apache-2.0 |

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Codex is the host with recorded same-session evidence. Other hosts are not accepted.
- Node.js 24 or newer is required by the embedded editor. The distributed package already contains the editor build; no Rust toolchain and no `npm install` are needed at runtime.
- Native file workflows use `soundcraft-cli`, which is not installed by this plugin. Query the actual version and command schema before running a recipe.
- The first Git-based launch needs network access or an existing verified editor cache. Complete release ZIPs can start offline from bundled assets.
- Source builds additionally need the project JavaScript dependencies, the Rust `wasm32` target, and a `wasm-bindgen` CLI matching `Cargo.lock`.

### From the plugin marketplace

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins
codex plugin add soundcraft@full-aigc-plugins
```

The repository also ships its own marketplace metadata (`soundcraft-marketplace`) pinned to `v0.1.0-dev.20261018.5`. Restart the host, open a new task, and ask for a read-only session inspection first.

## Quick start

1. Open the editor with an absolute workspace path: “Open SoundCraft for this folder and show me the current session.”
2. Wait for `editor_status` to report `attached: true` before editing. A successful tool response does not mean the page has rendered.
3. Work from real object IDs. Ask for one bounded operation, such as “on the Voice track, split at 2 seconds and add a 50 ms complementary linear crossfade”.
4. Save the project, reopen it in a new process, and re-inspect. Then bounce the mix and check the decoded audio rather than the dialog text.

```text
Inspect: List tracks, clips, sample rate, and any selection I should not reuse.
Edit: Cut the Voice clip at 2 s and crossfade 50 ms on both sides.
Level: Match two speakers to the same perceived level without clipping.
Deliver: Bounce a 48 kHz 24-bit WAV and confirm its length and format.
```

Direct CLI form for file tasks, using one argv argument per method:

```bash
soundcraft-cli info input.wav
soundcraft-cli run --in session.scraft --cmd 'session.inspect={"detail":"full"}' --save out.scraft
```

## What you can build

| Workflow | Built-in path | Verifiable output |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Clean up a podcast episode | `soundcraft-podcast-cleanup` | Edited speech, pauses, and loudness with a reopened project |
| Mix voice over music | `soundcraft-voice-over-mix` | Dialogue clarity and music bed checked as separate tracks |

`.codex-plugin/mcp.json` starts one stdio server, `soundcraft-editor`, from `ui/bootstrap.mjs`. The adapter adds three stable tools and passes through the pinned engine's command catalog.

Inside the session, the engine catalog in `ui/catalog.lock.json` provides `list_commands`, the `execute` wrapper, batch execution, session open/save, audio import, mix bounce, and UI automation tools. # dsh-multi-agent-gateway

**DSH 的多 Agent 通用 API 反代网关 Provider 插件。**

一个插件管起所有「AI Agent 平台」的账号：统一账号管理、每日签到、额度/积分拉取、
活动任务自动执行、多账号智能路由；同时把各平台的模型**按 Agent 分组**上报到 DSH
对话框的**原生模型选择器**，并在每个模型名后标注**积分消耗倍率**。

不是独立 Nginx，也不是外部代理进程 —— 请求全部在插件内部转发，账号凭证只存在本机。

## 界面：五页 + 浏览器登录

设置页现在是**独立一页**（设置 → 多 Agent 网关），内部按「你此刻要回答的问题」分五页：

| 页 | 回答什么问题 |
|---|---|
| **总览** | 现在健康吗？刚才那条花了多少？ |
| **账号** | 这个平台有哪些账号 / 模型？ |
| **任务** | 签到和活动任务跑得怎么样？ |
| **日志** | 刚才那次为什么失败？ |
| **设置** | 那些不常动的东西（含版本更新） |

**添加账号不用手抄 token**：账号页点「打开登录页」→ 浏览器里完成平台登录 → 回来点
「刷新登录状态」→ 插件自己去换 token 并建账号（token 不经过浏览器，加密落盘）。

| 平台 | 登录形态 |
|---|---|
| OpenCode | 设备码（显示 user_code，前端自动轮询） |
| WorkBuddy / 国际版 | 外链（`auth/state` → 打开登录页 → `auth/token?state=`） |
| Qoder / Qoder CN | 设备码 + PKCE |

> 外链形态**不自动轮询** —— 用户可能在浏览器里待几分钟，后台一直打上游纯属浪费。

**模型表**按「免费 → 厂商 → 倍率」排序，默认勾选免费模型（没有免费就全不勾），
每行可单独改上下文长度、可单独「测一次」，状态列显示 可用 / 地区受限 / 不可用 / 未探测。

## 💬 DeepSeek Harness 插件交流群

欢迎加入 **DeepSeek Harness 插件交流 QQ 群**——插件开发、模型接入、推理档位、
第三方厂商配置等话题都可以在这里交流，本插件的问题与建议也欢迎直接进群反馈：

> ## 🐧 QQ 群号：`1105449571`
>
> 打开 QQ → 搜索群号 **1105449571** 即可加入（进群请备注「dsh 插件」）

群内可交流：插件开发经验、模型接入与档位配置、DSH 使用技巧、新功能需求投票等。

---

## 它解决什么

| 你现在的麻烦 | 这个插件怎么办 |
|---|---|
| 有 5 个平台、十几个账号，每个平台一套登录/签到/查额度 | 一个配置页全管起来，按 Agent 分组 |
| 某个号限流了 / 额度用完了，会话当场报错 | 同 Agent 内自动换号重试，用户无感 |
| 每天要手动去点签到、领活动任务积分 | 定时任务自动跑，流水可查 |
| 模型下拉里一堆同名模型，看不出哪个贵 | 按 Agent 分组，后面缀 `(×2)` / `(免费)` |

## 支持情况

| Agent | 状态 | 签到 | 额度 | 模型 | 活动任务 | 对话 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenCode** | ✅ 完整实现 | 取决于上游¹ | ✅ | ✅ | 取决于上游¹ | ✅ 流式 + 思维链 |
| Qoder | 🧩 骨架 | — | — | — | — | — |
| Qoder CN | 🧩 骨架 | — | — | — | — | — |
| Trae | 🧩 骨架 | — | — | — | — | — |
| WorkBuddy | 🧩 骨架 | — | — | — | — | — |
| WorkBuddy International | 🧩 骨架 | — | — | — | — | — |

> ¹ **opencode.ai 官方 Console 没有签到接口，也没有活动任务接口。**
> 这两项是国内反代平台常见的形态，所以本插件把接口路径做成**可配置**的：
> 你填了 `upstream.checkInPath` / `tasksPath` 就真去调；没填就明确回报
> 「上游没有这个接口（这不是故障）」，**绝不伪造签到结果**。
> 详见 [`docs/OPENCODE-API.md`](docs/OPENCODE-API.md)。

### 「免费模型不要 key」——对，插件做到了**一个字段都不用填**

**不登录、不填 API key、不填凭证** —— 账号卡片里只填一个标签就完事，
模型选择器里选 `OpenCode · xxx (免费)` 直接聊。

为什么以前会 403、现在能过：上游那句 `FreeTierError`（*"can only be used from
within OpenCode"*）是**营销话术**，它实际校验的是**请求形状**。消融实验实测出来的
**过门三件事**：

| 条件 | 去掉会怎样 |
|---|---|
| `stream: true` | **403** —— 免费层只接受流式 |
| 请求里有一个叫 `read` 的工具 | **403** |
| 规范的 `x-opencode-session`（`ses_…` 降序编码） | **403** |

其余（`Authorization`、`x-opencode-request`、`x-opencode-project`）**去掉照样过**。

插件在「账号没有 key」时自动补齐这三样（`upstream.freeTierMode: 'auto'` 默认值），
`stream: true` 本来就是它的固定行为，`read` 工具 DSH 本来就发 —— 所以是真的零配置。
机制细节、实测报文、消融表见 [`docs/OPENCODE-API.md`](docs/OPENCODE-API.md) §1.5–1.6。

**实测证据**（`npm run test:free`）：空凭证账号 → 200 → 正文「收到」+
`reasoning_content` + usage，**全程没有任何 key**。

**边界**：匿名通道**只对免费模型有效**；付费模型在它上面会直接
`401 Missing API key`。要用付费模型就走登录/API key。上游随时可能再改门禁 ——
被拒时错误信息会把那三件事列出来，不会让你瞎试。

**另外**：模型目录完全免凭证，所以模型选择器里的分组与倍率
**一个账号都不加也能显示**，只是发不出请求。

「骨架」= 标准化接口**全部实现**，但默认返回「上游不支持」。语义明确、不静默失败；
填上真实的端点与凭证即可工作。扩展方法见 [`docs/EXTENDING.md`](docs/EXTENDING.md)。

## 快速开始

```powershell
# 1) 装进当前 profile（会自动应用 bundle patch）
dsh plugin --profile desktop add D:\AI\DeepseekPlugin\dsh-multi-agent-gateway

# 2) 重启 DSH 桌面端（客户端 bundle 要重新加载）

# 3) 打开 设置 → 插件 → 多 Agent 网关，填账号
```

详细步骤见 [`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md)。

## 文档地图

| 文档 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| [`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md) | 安装 / 卸载 / 升级 / 目录结构 / 常见安装问题 |
| [`docs/USAGE.md`](docs/USAGE.md) | 添加账号、看积分、配自动任务、调账号路由 |
| [`docs/MODELS.md`](docs/MODELS.md) | 模型分组与倍率标签是怎么进到 DSH 原生选择器的 |
| [`docs/OPENCODE-API.md`](docs/OPENCODE-API.md) | OpenCode 上游的真实接口事实（含核对过的端点表） |
| [`docs/EXTENDING.md`](docs/EXTENDING.md) | **新增一个 Agent 适配器要写什么**（含完整模板） |
| [`docs/ERROR-HANDLING.md`](docs/ERROR-HANDLING.md) | 账号降级、重试规则、任务失败与熔断 |
| [`docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`](docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md) | **已知问题 / 待修清单**（含验证步骤与排查顺序） |
| [`docs/NEXT-PHASE.md`](docs/NEXT-PHASE.md) | 本期刻意没做的功能，以及做它们需要的条件 |

## 架构（分层模块化）

```
                        ┌──────────────────────── DSH ────────────────────────┐
   对话请求 ──▶ ctx.llm ──▶ src/llm/adapter.ts（每 Agent 一个 provider 路由）
                        │            │                                    │
                        │            ▼                                    │
   模型选择器 ◀───────────│  src/runtime.ts（总装：模型缓存 / 分组 / 倍率标签）   │
                        │            │                                    │
   客户端配置页 ◀─ src/remote.ts ─┼─▶ core/router.ts  多账号路由（换号/降权/恢复）│
                        │            ├─▶ core/scheduler.ts 定时任务管理器    │
                        │            ├─▶ core/tasks.ts  活动任务引擎         │
                        │            └─▶ core/accounts.ts 账号（AES-256-GCM）│
                        │                       │                          │
                        │                       ▼                          │
   工具 ◀────────────────┘            src/adapters/*.ts（每 Agent 一个适配器） │
                        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**新增 Agent 只需要在 `src/adapters/` 加一个文件 + 在 `adapters/index.ts` 加一行。**
核心调度（路由 / 定时 / 任务 / 网关 / UI）一行都不用改。

## 数据落在哪

默认 `<DSH_HOME>/multi-agent-gateway`（`DSH_HOME` 一般是 `~/.dsh`）：

| 文件 | 内容 | 丢了会怎样 |
|---|---|---|
| `.master-key` | AES-256-GCM 主密钥（0600） | **账号密文再也解不开**，要重录 |
| `accounts.enc.json` | 账号与凭证（整份加密） | 要重录账号 |
| `state.json` | 额度缓存、健康、模型缓存、任务游标（明文、无敏感信息） | 重算，无损失 |
| `task-log.jsonl` | 任务执行流水（可删） | 历史记录没了 |

**安全边界（说清楚，不吹）**：密文与密钥分文件，防的是「配置被云同步 / 被 grep 到明文
token / 备份泄露」。它**不是硬件密钥库** —— 能读该目录的本机进程同样能读密钥。

## 开发

```powershell
node scripts/build.mjs      # TypeScript → lib/（零依赖，用 Node 自带的类型擦除）
npm test                    # 单元测试 72 + 客户端契约 15 + 冒烟
node test/live-opencode.mjs # 真机管线：打真实 OpenCode 目录核倍率（需要联网，只读公开接口）
```

改完 `src/` **必须重新构建**（`lib/` 是产物）；改完 `client/` 也要重跑构建，
然后重启 DSH（宿主在启动时扫描 `dsh.client` 声明）。

### 已验证

| 验证 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/build.mjs` | 26 个 TS 文件 → `lib/`，零不可擦除语法 |
| 单元测试 | **72/72** 通过 |
| 客户端契约测试 | **24/24** 通过（端点、描述符、volatile 路径、真 `apply(ctx)`、**无参端点零参数**、真渲染 ModelList） |
| 假宿主冒烟 | 通过（provider 路由 / 5 个工具 / **模型上报策略真的改变选择器内容** / 密文落盘） |
| **真机免费层**（`npm run test:free`，联网） | **空凭证账号 → 200 → 正文「收到」+ 思维链 + usage，全程零 key** |
| 真机管线（`npm run test:live`，联网） | 真实模型目录 + 倍率；设备码登录实测发起成功、未授权正确返回 `pending` |
| 真实 DSH 进程（headless profile） | 通过（**零 `did not activate`、零配置校验错误**） |
| **真实浏览器**（Edge + 真 web profile） | 通过 —— 客户端 bundle 在 boot combo 里、`apply` 正常激活、控制台零本插件错误 |

### 模型不是全塞进去：默认只报**免费**的

上游实测 85 个模型，全进下拉的话免费那几个会被淹没。所以每个 Agent 有一份上报策略
（设置页里就是三个按钮 + 一个带搜索的勾选列表）：`free`（默认）/ `selected` / `all`。
详见 [`docs/MODELS.md`](docs/MODELS.md) §6.5。

plugins.description: Command resolution forensics: which file a command actually runs, what it shadows, and whether the copies agree.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-which

**Command resolution forensics for DeepSeek Harness.** When you type `node`, a shell answers with a rule that is longer than people remember — PATH order, then PATHEXT on Windows or the executable bit elsewhere, with builtins short-circuiting the whole thing. `dsh-which` reports what that rule actually decided, what it shadowed, what shape PATH itself is in, and whether the copies behind one name agree on a version.

Every failure it names is silent. The command runs; it is just not the one you meant.

```
dsh-which · node
  winner:   C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
  kind:     native binary
  from:     PATH[0]  C:\Program Files\nodejs
  size:     84MB
  modified: 2025-11-03T09:14:00.000Z
  version:  v24.13.0  (--version)
  searched: 9 PATH entries

  shadowed — 1 other directory holds this name:
    PATH[6]  C:\Users\me\scoop\shims\node.EXE  native binary  84MB
      ↳ reports v20.11.1

  ⚠ the copies behind this name report different versions — the one that runs is the one at PATH[0].
```

That last block is the whole reason this exists. Two Node installations, one on PATH, and nothing anywhere tells you which one a command gets.

## Why not just run `which`

1. **`which` does not exist on Windows**, and where it does exist it answers a narrower question. It reports the file it found; it does not report the file it skipped.
2. **`which` inherits the rules under investigation.** Shelling out to a resolver to explain resolution means trusting the resolver you are debugging. The rules here are reimplemented as pure functions over an injected filesystem (`lib/resolve.js`), so they are testable against fixtures instead of against whatever is installed on the test machine.
3. **Shell builtins are not files.** `which cd` on most systems walks every PATH entry to report something that has nothing to do with what runs. This plugin says `builtin` and explains that PATH was never consulted.
4. **The interesting output is the shadowed copy.** "What runs" is one line. "What else answers to this name, and why is it not running" is the diagnosis — a stale global install behind a fresh local one, a `.cmd` shim in front of a real binary, a file that exists but was never made executable.
5. **Reporting is the whole job.** There is no PATH-editing tool here. A plugin that silently rewrites PATH is a plugin that breaks a machine.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin add https://github.com/11111353535/dsh-which
```

From a checkout instead of a git host, pass the absolute path:

```sh
dsh plugin add /absolute/path/to/dsh-which
```

Optional configuration, in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: which
  name: 'dsh-which'
  config:
    probeByDefault: false        # run a version probe on every resolve
    probeShadowedByDefault: false # probe the shadowed copies too
    probeTimeoutMs: 4000
    maxSweepFiles: 400
    runtimes: [node, npm, pnpm, python, git]
```

| key | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `probeTimeoutMs` | `4000` | How long a version probe may take before it is abandoned. |
| `probeByDefault` | `false` | Probe every resolve without being asked. Slower, explains more. |
| `probeShadowedByDefault` | `false` | Probe the shadowed copies too. Multiplies the process spawns. |
| `maxSweepFiles` | `400` | Files examined in one sweep, so a huge directory cannot stall a session. |
| `runtimes` | node, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, python, python3, pip, pip3, uv, git, rg, fd, make, pwsh, bash | Commands the environment report resolves. |

Probing is off by default because it spawns processes, and a diagnostic that costs four seconds on every call is a diagnostic people turn off.

## Tools

### `which_resolve`

Resolve one command and report what runs, what it shadowed, and — on request — what each copy reports as its version.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string, **required** | A name (`node`) or a path (`./build.sh`, `C:\tools\x.exe`). |
| `probe` | boolean | Run the winner with a version flag. |
| `probeShadowed` | boolean | Probe the shadowed copies too, so versions can be compared. |

A name that resolves to nothing is an answer, not an error:

```
dsh-which · build
  not found
  the name exists on PATH but nothing with that name is runnable
  searched: 45 PATH entries

  the name exists, but nothing with it can run:
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        … and 37 more
```

The count is the finding; the enumeration is the evidence, and past eight directories the evidence stops being read. The lines that save an hour are the second and third: the name *is* on PATH, the file simply cannot run. On POSIX that means no executable bit — a shell walks right past it into later PATH entries, or fails.

An explicit path never consults PATH, and the report says so:

```
dsh-which · /repo/scripts/build.sh
  winner:   /repo/scripts/build.sh
  kind:     script
  from:     given as a path, PATH was not consulted
  size:     2.3KB
  searched: 0 PATH entries
```

### `which_path`

The shape of PATH itself: every entry in resolution order, with duplicates, entries whose directory is gone, and entries containing an unexpanded variable.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `showNoise` | boolean | Include `/usr/bin`, `/bin` and friends, omitted by default as uninformative. |
| `limit` | number | Maximum entries listed. Defaults to 40. |

```
dsh-which · PATH
  9 entries · 8 unique directories
  1 duplicate entry · 1 dead entry

  entries, in resolution order:
    [ 0] C:\Program Files\nodejs
    [ 1] C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\npm
    [ 2] C:\Windows\system32
    [ 3] C:\Windows
    [ 4] C:\tools\git\cmd
    [ 5] C:\Program Files\nodejs  — dup of [0]
    [ 6] C:\Users\me\scoop\shims
    [ 7] D:\old-python\Scripts  — missing
    [ 8] C:\Users\me\bin

  Duplicates are usually an installer that prepends itself on every run. Harmless until you edit "the" entry and two copies of it remain.

  Dead entries are skipped silently by every shell, so an uninstalled toolchain leaves a hole that only shows up when its command fails.
```

A dead entry is invisible by construction: shells skip it without a word, so the hole only surfaces later as "command not found" for something that was there yesterday. An unexpanded `%USERPROFILE%` is worse — it can never resolve, no matter what the variable is set to.

### `which_env`

One page describing the command environment: platform, shell, working directory, PATH findings, PATHEXT, and where each common runtime resolves from.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | number | Maximum runtimes listed. Defaults to 30. |

```
dsh-which · environment
  platform: win32  arch x64  node v24.13.0
  shell:    pwsh.exe  (C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe)
  cwd:      C:\repo
  PATH:     9 entries · 8 unique
            1 duplicate · 1 dead
  PATHEXT:  .COM .EXE .BAT .CMD

  resolved runtimes:
    · node  C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
    · npm  C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD
    · pnpm  C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\npm\pnpm.CMD
    · git  C:\tools\git\cmd\git.EXE
    ✗ python  not found

  1 runtime(s) exist in more than one place on PATH: node
```

The shell line matters more than it looks. `pwsh` and `cmd` disagree about builtins and about `.ps1`, so a report that names the wrong shell is a report nobody should trust.

### `which_sweep`

Sweep a directory of scripts and report, for each name that looks like a command, whether the copy in *that* directory is the one that would run.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | string, **required** | Absolute, or relative to the workspace. |
| `limit` | number | Maximum rows listed. Defaults to 60. |

```
dsh-which · sweep C:\repo\scripts
  3 command(s)
  1 resolve outside this directory (shown with ↪)
  1 do not resolve at all

  ↪ build.cmd  → C:\tools\build\build.cmd
  · deploy.cmd  C:\repo\scripts\deploy.cmd
  ✗ smoke.cmd  does not resolve

  A ↪ means a copy in this di

--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.readme_text:
DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. The [**wiki**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki) is the user-facing guide: [getting started](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Getting-Started), [connecting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Connecting), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Troubleshooting), a [feature tour](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Feature-Tour) and an [FAQ](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/FAQ). --- ## Screenshots | Connect | Chat | Trajectory | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | | | | | Recent harnesses with live reachability, LAN discovery, manual `host:port`, auto-connect. | Streamed turns, a glyph per tool, expandable tool cards, permission picker. | The same session as a per-turn ledger with usage totals. | | Session details | Subagents | |:--:|:--:| | | | | Context breakdown, goal, plan mode, background jobs, queued turns, host info, session-log export. | The subagent catalog — open a child's transcript, follow up, or interrupt it. | ## Features - Connecting — finds a harness on your Wi-Fi with an active subnet scan and a readiness handshake, remembers hosts and probes them for liveness on the way in, takes a manual `host:port`, handles loopback for same-device setups, and auto-connects when you tell it to (last used, LAN, or same device). - Navigation — the drawers work like Discord's: swipe right from the left edge for the workspace-grouped chat list, swipe left to close it, swipe left from the right edge for the session details panel. - Chat — streamed turns with reasoning disclosure, markdown, terminal/diff/read/search/web tool cards, a queue dock where you can edit, remove or steer a queued turn, history paging, and multi-photo and file attachments. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. The automatic check also runs again when you come back to the app after a few hours. - Workspace links in replies drawn as file and folder pills; a folder opens in Files. - A redesigned Details panel, Workspace screen and Settings, with archived sessions on a tab of their own. ### Added in 0.14.0 - A `/` menu above the composer with the session's commands and skills. - A picker for the dsh-rewind plugin's `/rewind` and `/undo` that asks for confirmation before it restores files. The transcript hides what a rewind withdrew and marks the cut. ### Added in 0.13.0 - Automation catalog, timing edits, delivery history and session shortcuts. - Plugin installation, updates, toggles, removal, progress and recovery. Create plugin stages an unsent draft with the Creator preset when the host offers it. - Timed questions, continued replies, saved answer drafts and reopenable plans. - Draft text and file, folder and session references saved across app restarts. - Model search, YAML document properties and multiline goal editing. - Reverse-proxy path support and tool argument previews while the model is writing. ## Requirements - Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26). - A running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) at `0.2.1-alpha.2`, the protocol baseline for DSH Mobile `0.16.0`. Existing protocol fallbacks remain for `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.x` and `0.1.6-alpha.x`; new management features need host support. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [0.13.0 validation status](docs/VALIDATION-0.13.0.md) for what has been checked on this baseline. ## Quick start 1. Install the latest APK from [Releases](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/releases/latest). 2. Open the app and choose how to connect. Relay and local network are two different setups, not two settings of one, so pick the one that matches wha

# dsh-tool-planner

A DSH skill that helps non-programmers plan and build a tool by interview.

It walks the user through how they do the task by hand today, one plain-language step at a time, turning each step into a flowchart node. Then a short round of automation questions, a plain-language plan, and explicit approval before building.

## Install

**Desktop app:** open **Plugins → Add Plugin**, paste the source below, click install, then restart the app.

```
github:WasifAlamDip/dsh-fde-tool-planner
```

**Terminal:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:WasifAlamDip/dsh-fde-tool-planner
```

If `dsh` is not on your PATH, put `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` in place of `dsh`. Restart dsh after installing.

To pin a release, add a tag: `github:WasifAlamDip/dsh-fde-tool-planner#v0.1.0`.

## Usage

Describe what you want in 3–4 lines. Answer in plain language — no technical knowledge needed.

## Uninstall

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-tool-planner
```

## Credits

Built by [Wasif Alam Dip](https://github.com/WasifAlamDip).

## License

# dsh-session-cleaner

A **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** plugin — host half and Web client half in one bundle — that adds two
things to the DSH Web GUI:

1. **Delete a conversation** from the sidebar session menu, with a confirmation dialog.
2. **Quote / Ask from the right-click menu** — select text in a chat message, then right-click. The
   plugin takes over the context menu and shows **Copy / Quote / Ask**, with Copy first, exactly where
   the native menu item used to be:
   - **Copy** writes the selection to the clipboard (the same action as before, now drawn by us).
   - **Quote** inserts a Markdown quote block (role + turn metadata) into the composer.
   - **Ask** sends the selection plus your question to a *concurrent subagent* and streams the answer
     into the right sidebar, without interrupting the main conversation.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

---

## Features

| Surface | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` | **Delete session** — stops a running session (flush + detach), detaches it from the workspace registry, invalidates its projection cache, physically removes the session directory, cleans its spill directory, cascades to its `origin: subagent` children (fork branches are never cascaded), then broadcasts `api-session/removed`. |
| `shell.overlay` | Selection **right-click menu**: **Copy** (clipboard) / **Quote** (insert into the composer) / **Ask** (concurrent subagent question). The menu is drawn by the plugin because the desktop app builds its native context menu in the Electron main process, which a renderer plugin cannot extend; `preventDefault()` on `contextmenu` keeps the native menu from popping. |
| `sidebar.right.pane.tab` | **Follow-up** tab: streams the ask subagent's answer (reasoning + text) in the right sidebar. |

### Ask reuses one subagent

Every question does **not** spawn a new subagent. The plugin keeps a single continuable subagent
labelled `ask` per parent session and delivers the next question to it (discovering the existing one
through the official `subagents.listChildren()` catalog, so it survives a host restart).

### Scoped auto-compaction for the ask subagent

Because the reused `ask` subagent's context grows with every question, the host registers its own
`agent/pre-step` listener that calls `ctx.compaction.compactIfNeeded(agent, "pressure", signal)`
**only for this plugin's own ask subagents**. Global automatic compaction stays off
(`compaction-basic` is mounted with `auto: false`) — the main conversation is unaffected.

---

## Install

The plugin is a normal DSH bundle. Add it to your profile's `package.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@local/dsh-session-cleaner-host": "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-session-cleaner-host"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        // …
        "@local/dsh-session-cleaner-host"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The package name must be used consistently in three places:

- `package.json` → `name`
- `client.js` → `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: "…" })`
- the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` entry

Then add the compaction backend to your profile patch layer
(`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`), which is applied **after** every bundle layer:

```yaml
# Compaction backend for the ask subagent's scoped auto-compaction.
# `auto: false` keeps GLOBAL automatic compaction off; the plugin calls
# ctx.compaction.compactIfNeeded() itself, scoped to its own ask subagents.
- id: compaction-basic
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic"
  disabled: false
  config:
    auto: false
```

> Keep this row in the **profile** patch, not in this package's bundle patch: installing a plugin
> must not silently enable another package for the whole profile.

Restart DSH after changing host-side code, then reload the page. Verify which build is live:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dsh-session-cleaner/version
# {"ok":true,"name":"dsh-session-cleaner","build":"…","features":{…}}
```

---

## Usage

**Quote / Ask**

1. Select some text in a chat message.
2. Right-click inside the selection.
3. The context menu opens with **Copy / Quote / Ask** (Copy first, then a separator).
4. *Quote* appends a quoted block to the composer. *Ask* swaps the menu for a question box; send it
   and the **Follow-up** tab opens in the right sidebar with the streamed answer.

Right-clicking in the composer, or right-clicking without a selection, keeps the normal system menu
(cut / paste / select all).

**Delete a conversation**

Sidebar session row → `⋯` → **Delete session**. Deleting the currently open session stops it and
switches the page to a new session.

---

## HTTP API

All routes are served by the plugin's host half (same-origin, browser cookie auth):

| Method | Path | Body | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-session-cleaner/version` | — | Which build is live (diagnostics). |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-cleaner/ask` | `{ sessionId, text }` | Deliver a question to the reused `ask` subagent, creating it once if needed. |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-cleaner/delete-session` | `{ sessionId }` | Delete a whole session (and cascade to its subagent children). |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-cleaner/delete-subagent` | `{ childId, parentId }` | Delete one direct subagent child. Guarded by a lineage check. |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-cleaner/terminate-children` | `{ sessionId }` | Drain every continuable descendant of a session. |

---

## Design notes and hard-won constraints

These are the constraints that shape the implementation. Several of them were established by reading
the shipped DSH sources, and getting any of them wrong produces silent data loss.

1. **DSH exposes no "delete a session" API.** `sessions`, `sessionPersistence`,
   `sessionProjectionCache` and `sessionController` are all append-only; the persistence seam documents
   *"Nothing deletes session files … the seam has no deletion API."* This plugin therefore performs
   deliberate on-disk surgery — and compensates with strict identity checks.
2. **Never rewrite another session's log.** The plugin originally rewrote the parent log to drop a
   `subagent/catalog` row. Session logs are append-only and may be written concurrently by the host, so
   a read → filter → atomic-rename could truncate a conversation. `rewriteParentLog` now defaults to
   **`false`**.
3. **Session directory lookup is identity-verified.** Any candidate directory must yield a log whose
   header `id` equals the requested session id; the plugin never falls back to guessing.
4. **`subagent/catalog` is append-only.** There is no supported way to remove a row, and removing the
   child's session behind a live row produces a dangling entry. The plugin does not touch catalog rows.
5. **Subagent operations are lineage-guarded.** `delete-subagent` refuses unless
   `header.parentSession === parentId && header.origin === "subagent"`, and refuses
   `childId === parentId` — without that check, "delete the subagent" can delete the conversation you
   are looking at.
6. **Compaction needs a *live idle* agent.** `compaction.compactNow(agent, signal)` takes a
   `ManualCompactAgentContext` (it needs `runMaintenance()`), but a continuable subagent is **not
   resident after its turn settles**. There is therefore no supported way to compact a *finished*
   subagent on demand; compaction only works at `agent/pre-step`, while the turn is open and the agent
   is alive. That is why the plugin hooks `agent/pre-step` instead of offering a button.
7. **Self-contained by design.** The host half imports **only Node builtins** — no `@deepseek-ai/*`
   runtime dependency, so the plugin cannot shadow the official packages in a profile's
   `node_modules`. `package.json` declares no dependencies at all.
8. **Selections are quoted verbatim** and capped at 2000 characters; a selection spanning two messages
   or inside a streaming message is ignored.

---

## Tests

```powershell
npm test
```

Two self-contained suites, no DSH, no browser and no real session data:

| Suite | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `test/internals.test.mjs` | host half: zstd session-log framing, projection keys, log decode/encode |
| `tes

## dsh-auto-upgrade

**来源：纯原创**（`package.json` 的 `repository` 已指向本仓库 `directory: dsh-auto-upgrade`）。
**改动：—**（没有上游）。

给 dsh 的 Web UI 加一个**自升级**入口：当天首次打开页面时自动检测 dsh 新版本与已装插件的兼容性，
用一个**不打断当前工作**的浮层提示；用户点「升级」后才走完整链路。

![设置页](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/screenshots/settings.png)

![浮层](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/screenshots/overlay.png)

### 它做什么

1. **当天首次打开自动检测**：宿主按本地日期幂等，同一天多标签页 / 刷新只真正检测一次。
2. **检测两件事**：npm 上的 dsh 新版本；已装插件对**目标版本**的兼容性（用官方 `evaluatePluginCompatibility`，不是自己写范围匹配）。
3. **不打断工作的浮层**：右下角卡片，只占自己的位置；可「稍后」「不再提示」。
4. **点升级才动手**：会话门禁 → 插件门禁 → 备份 `~/.dsh` → 停服 → `npm install -g` → 对版 + 组合冒烟 → 重启交接。
5. **回滚与重启**：重装指定旧版本；或只重启服务。设置页还有本机体检、插件兼容表、升级 / 重启日志。

### 关键设计

- **双面插件，无构建步骤**：宿主半边 `lib/index.js` 用 cordis 注册 `/api/dsh-auto-upgrade/*` 路由族；
  浏览器半边 `lib/client.js` 手写并包在 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})` 里，注册
  `shell.overlay` 浮层与 `settings.section` 设置页。
- **变更必须脱离进程**：`npm install -g` 覆盖的正是宿主此刻在运行的那棵树，而「停服」就是杀掉宿主自己。
  所以宿主只做「门禁 → 备份 → 落 payload → fork detached helper → `exit 0`」，停服 / 安装 / 对版 / 冒烟 / 拉起
  都在生成的 POSIX sh helper 里。
- **故意不声明 `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peerDependencies**：否则升级之后，平台闸门会把「负责升级 dsh 的插件」
  自己判成不兼容（自锁）。本包只声明 `react`（浏览器半边需要）。
- **安全边界**：路由族能读 npm、重写全局安装树、覆盖 `~/.dsh`、结束本进程，所以一律 loopback-only
  （以 socket 地址为准，不信任 `X-Forwarded-For`），并且**有副作用的一律 POST**。
- **UI 吃 dsh 的设计 token**：字体 `--dsw-font-*`、圆角 `--dsw-radius-*`、语义色 `--dsw-alias-state-*`，
  数值逐条对齐官方实现。详见包内 README 的「UI 风格契约」。

### 两条门禁（默认策略）

| 情况 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| 有会话正在执行 | `409`，前端弹警告；用户确认后可带 `force` 继续（**仅警告**） |
| 目标版本与已装插件不兼容 | `409`，**拒绝升级且不可绕过**——先升级 / 移除那个插件，或为它写精确版本豁免 |

> 豁免是按「插件@版本 → dsh 版本」精确匹配的：为 `0.2.0-rc.2` 写的豁免，升级到别的版本时**自动失效**，
> 那个插件会立刻出现在「不兼容」里。这正是本插件要提前告诉你的信息。

### 已知限制（诚实清单）

- **真机的安装 / 升级 / 重启链路尚未执行**（属于需要用户点头的闸门）；只读半边与门禁已在真机验证。
- 只支持 macOS / Linux：helper 是 POSIX sh 脚本。
- `POST /plugins/action`（写豁免 / 禁用插件）尚未接线，如实返回 `501`；`GET /notes` 已实现。
- 暂不做「静默自动升级」：`policy.mode` 只接受 `notify`。

- [验收报告：逐条证据 + 明确没验证什么](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/acceptance/dsh-auto-upgrade-acceptance.md)

## 安装 / 卸载

```sh
# 安装（<目录> 用仓库内的目录名，路径按实际 clone 位置调整）
dsh plugin --profile web add /Users/gubin/workspace/self-dsh-plugins/<目录>

# 卸载

- `add` 时若插件 `package.json` 声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`，会自动挂上 patch 层，**无需手改**

```sh
# 跑 4 个插件的测试 / check / typecheck（缺 node_modules 的插件会明确跳过，不算失败）
scripts/pipeline/check-all.sh
scripts/pipeline/check-all.sh dsh-auto-upgrade dsh-plugin-product-subagents   # 只跑指定插件

# 在一次性 $DSH_HOME 里验证插件能被 profile 正确安装 + 组合（绝不触碰真实 ~/.dsh）
scripts/pipeline/install-check.sh
scripts/pipeline/install-check.sh dsh-plugin-product-subagents
```

- **本仓库的「交付物」不是线上服务，而是「插件被本机 DSH profile 正确装配」**——对应 `install-check.sh`，
  它每个插件新建一个 `mktemp -d` 的 `DSH_HOME`，`pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@<当前版本> plugin --profile headless add <插件>`

- 只读状态一览：`scripts/pipeline/status.sh`。
- CI（`.github/workflows/ci.yml`）只跑测试 + `node --check`，**零部署步骤**；`dsh-im-bridge-workspaces`
  那一项 `install: false`，即跳过安装 / 测试 / typecheck，只跑语法门禁。

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-cache-report

[![CI](https://github.com/youran0faust/dsh-cache-report/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/youran0faust/dsh-cache-report/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.15-brightgreen)

> **命中率从 96% 掉到 80%，是谁吃的？**

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）提示缓存命中率与工具块成本报表。一条命令告诉你：今天的 token 花在哪、哪次操作最贵、哪个插件在占位。

> 中文 | [English](README.en.md) · MIT · 零运行时依赖

## 它回答什么问题

大模型的输入分「命中缓存」和「未命中」两种价钱（DeepSeek 官方约 **1 : 10**）。缓存按**前缀**精确匹配，而请求的排布是：

```
[工具定义]   ← 一变，后面全部作废
[系统提示]
[历史消息…]  ← 缓存主要靠这里
[本轮新内容] ← 只有这里应该按未命中计费
```

于是：**在长会话中途装一个插件、启停一个组件、切一次权限档，工具定义就变了——此后整段上下文（系统提示 + 全部历史）会按全价重算一遍。**

多数人只看到命中率掉了，却不知道是谁吃的。这个工具就是回答这个的。

## 安装

前置：DSH（`@deepseek-ai/dsh`）+ Node.js ≥ 20。

### 方式 A：作为 DSH 插件（推荐）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:youran0faust/dsh-cache-report#main
```

重启 DSH（或依赖 profile 的 `patchReload: live` 热加载），然后在会话输入框打：

```
/cache-report
```

**它只注册斜杠命令、不注册任何工具**——因此**不改变工具表、不会破坏你自己的缓存**。常驻零成本。

### 方式 B：独立脚本（不需要插件机制）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/youran0faust/dsh-cache-report.git
node dsh-cache-report/lib/report.mjs today
```

零运行时依赖，只用 Node 内置模块（`node:fs` / `node:path` / `node:zlib` / `node:os`）。

## 命令

| 输入 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `/cache-report` | 不带参数 = `today`：今天的命中率 + 大额重算归因 |
| `/cache-report days 7` | 近 7 天趋势表 |
| `/cache-report tools 30` | 工具块成本 / 按插件拆分 / 从未被调用的死重 |
| `/cache-report before-after 24` | 近 24 小时：工具表变化时间线 + 重算代价 + 真实台账花费 |
| `/cache-report debug 7` | 格式自检：DSH 会话格式是否仍符合预期 |
| `/cache-report help` | 用法 |

独立脚本用法相同：`node lib/report.mjs days 7`。
