# Balance Bucket · 余额水桶

**A little bucket that drains while your DeepSeek API balance is being spent.**

![Six bucket states: full, pouring, low, refilled, unreadable, and dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/youchai2016/dsh-plugin-token-bucket/v0.1.1/docs/images/bucket-states.png)

一只挂在窗口角落的小水桶。**水是你的余额，漏出去的是正在花的钱。**

Version 0.1.1.

## What it does

- **The water level is your real balance.** It reads `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` with the same `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` that DSH chats with, so the bucket shows the money you actually have.
- **The water is two layers, because the money is.** Granted balance (赠送) floats on top of topped-up balance (充值). DeepSeek deducts the granted wallet first, so you watch the pale layer empty before the deep one moves.
- **The tap opens while money moves.** The stream and its droplets are proportional to the burn rate over the last three minutes — the tool for watching a `vibe coding` session eat your credit.
- **The bucket is as tall as the highest balance it has ever seen.** It starts full, and a top-up makes it taller rather than overflowing.
- **A failed read never lies.** If the balance cannot be read, the water stays where it was, the tap shuts, and the outline turns amber. It never empties the bucket to show an error.

Move it, resize it, tuck it away — right-click for settings, drag to reposition, arrow keys to nudge.

## Reading the bucket

| Look | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Pale layer on top | Granted balance (spent first) |
| Deep layer below | Topped-up balance |
| Blue water | Above 30% of the highest balance seen |
| Amber water | Between 10% and 30% |
| Red water, gentle wobble | Below 10% |
| Amber outline, no stream | The last read failed; the level is the last known one |
| Grey water, `—` | No API key configured, or the key was rejected |

Hover the bucket for the numbers, or open the settings panel for balance, granted/topped-up split, spent since start, added since start, burn rate, bucket size and the age of the last reading.

## Install

Package page: [dsh-plugin-token-bucket on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-token-bucket).

```text
dsh-plugin-token-bucket
```

Or pin this release:

```text
github:youchai2016/dsh-plugin-token-bucket#v0.1.0
```

The plugin needs the credential DSH already manages for chat. If the Models page has a working DeepSeek API key, the bucket works; if not, it says so instead of guessing.

## Privacy and runtime boundaries

- The API key is resolved through DSH's credential service on every poll and is **never** stored, logged, echoed in an error, or sent to the client half. The browser half never talks to the balance service itself.
- **One** outbound request exists: a read-only `GET` on the documented balance endpoint. No model calls, no telemetry, no listening port, no third-party service.
- Nothing about your conversations is read. This plugin subscribes to **no** session events, so it cannot see prompts, replies or tool output.
- Preferences and history live in the browser's local storage. The plugin never writes your DSH profile.

## Honest limits

- The burn rate is **estimated from balance deltas**, not from token counts: the balance moves in whole cents (¥0.01), so the reading is a rolling three-minute average rather than a per-request figure. It is deliberately not a billing statement.
- Polling is adaptive: every 5 seconds for two minutes after money moves, then 20 seconds, then once a minute while nothing happens. Change calls from other devices or tools are also visible, because they move the same balance.
- Prices, bonuses and the split between granted and topped-up balance are whatever the API reports. The bucket does not compute costs from a price list.
- Balances are read for one currency, preferring CNY.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
npm test
```

`preview/index.html` is a single offline file: open it in a browser, no server and no network needed. Its buttons fabricate balance samples, so every state can be inspected without an API key.

The Host half is bundled to `lib/index.js`, the strict browser/Host contract to `lib/remote.js`, and the browser half to `lib/client.js` by `pnpm run build`. Prebuilt files are committed so a Git install needs no build step.

## License

Code is [MIT](LICENSE). No third-party artwork is bundled: the bucket is drawn with CSS and one inline SVG.

plugins.description: DSH 技能中心：查看、开关、新建、按链接安装、删除（进回收站可恢复）DSH 技能。
plugins.readme_text:
# @suifengshiqu/skill-center

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

**Skill Center** adds one page to the DSH Web client where you can see every skill DSH can load from your own directories, read one, switch it on or off, create one, install one from a link, and delete one into a trash you can restore from.

It is a third-party DSH plugin, not an official DeepSeek product. Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

![The Skill Center panel, open over the composer](docs/shots/list.png)

## Screenshots

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![The skill list](docs/shots/list.png) | ![Creating a skill](docs/shots/create.png) |
| **The list** — every skill DSH can load, with its switch, its provenance and its problems. The row above it is where a link goes. | **Creating one** — name, description and body, written into whichever destination is selected. |
| ![The trash](docs/shots/trash.png) | ![The delete confirmation](docs/shots/confirm.png) |
| **The trash** — what was deleted, where it came from, and one button to put it back. | **Deleting** — the confirmation says plainly that the skill goes to the trash, because a reversible delete is a different promise from an erase. |

The screenshots are rendered from the shipped browser bundle over the Host's own
`Modal` stylesheet, so the layout, colours and scrollbar are the ones the application
produces; only the surrounding application window is left out. `scripts/dev/render-shots.mjs`
regenerates them, in either theme.

## Where it appears

Two entry points, both opening the same page over one shared store:

- **Settings → Skill Center** — the settings section, so it sits with the rest of the configuration.
- **A `Skills` button in the composer**, in the input row beside the permission chip. It opens the page in a modal, which is the quick path for switching a skill on or off mid-task.

The composer button lives in `conversation.input.left`. That is the only composer seat a plugin may extend: the permission chip (`conversation.input.permission`) and the model picker (`conversation.input.model`) are `single` seats their own plugins already hold, so nothing can be inserted between them. The button also cannot deep-link to its settings section — `openSection` is internal to the settings shell — so it opens the page directly instead.

Both entries follow the Host's theme:

![The same panel in the light theme](docs/shots/list-light.png)

## What it does

- **Lists** the skills under `$DSH_HOME/skills` (default `~/.dsh/skills`), any directory the profile adds through `customSkillDirs`, and the current project's `<project>/.dsh/skills`.
- **Shows details** for one skill: description, path, frontmatter block and instruction body.
- **Searches** by name or description, and can hide the switched-off skills.
- **Switches a skill on or off** without losing it: everything else about the file, including your own frontmatter keys, is left alone.
- **Creates a skill** from a name, a description and a body.
- **Installs a skill from a link** — a GitHub repository, a `/tree/` path inside one, a `.zip`, or a single `SKILL.md`.
- **Deletes a skill into a trash**, and restores it from there.
- **Writes new skills where you choose** — the destination control offers every directory the profile makes available, and the host accepts nothing else.
- **Reports problems** the host would silently skip, such as a missing `description` or a name that is not kebab-case.
- Follows the Host's light or dark theme.

### Where new skills are written

The destinations come from the Host, not from the panel: `GET /roots` answers with the
profile's configured `customSkillDirs` followed by the default `$DSH_HOME/skills`. The
browser offers exactly that list, and `POST /create` and `POST /install` refuse a
directory outside it — so "choose where to write" does not become "write anywhere". With
one destination the control is a sentence; with several, each is a button, because the
path is the point.

### Where deletion is allowed to reach

Removing something the user wrote is the one destructive thing here, so it is bounded:

- **Only DSH's own skills.** The trash covers the global roots (the DSH home and any `customSkillDirs`). A project root — `<project>/.dsh/skills`, which is under version control — is never touched: Skill Center may switch such a skill on or off, but it will not move it out of a repository.
- **Only skills DSH can actually load.** A skill with broken frontmatter may have been misread, which is a reason to leave it alone rather than to move it.
- **Never through a link.** A symbolic link, or a Windows junction (which `lstat` reports as an ordinary directory), is refused by comparing the resolved path with the requested one.
- **Never a plain erase.** The bundle is moved into `~/.dsh/skill-center/trash` with a record of where it came from, and the panel can put it back byte-for-byte. Emptying the trash is a separate, confirmed action.
- **Never a half-move.** Everything is validated before anything moves, and a move that cannot be recorded is rolled back. Because `rename` cannot cross volumes, a failed move falls back to copy-then-remove — copy first, so a failure leaves the original in place.

### What installing a link will and will not do

The download is treated as hostile input: entry paths may not escape the target, a bundle must have a `SKILL.md` with a name DSH accepts and a description DSH requires, an existing name is refused rather than overwritten, and nothing is written until every one of those checks has passed. Private archives and Zip64 are refused. Links to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `.local`) are not fetched, and a single download is capped at 8 MB and 800 entries.

### Which layouts are discovered

Matching the Host's own filesystem provider exactly, a skill is a directory bundle `<name>/SKILL.md` or a flat `<name>.md`, **at the top level of a skills root**. Nested `**/SKILL.md` is deliberately not discovered.

This matters when installing from a GitHub download: a repository ZIP extracts to one folder, and copying *that* folder into `~/.dsh/skills` leaves every bundle one level too deep, where neither DSH nor this panel will find it. Move the bundle folders themselves into the skills root.

## What it does not do

- No other agents' directories (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …).
- No Git repositories, no skill marketplace, no automatic updates.
- No creating or importing skills.
- No Trash.
- Nothing outside the two roots above is ever read or written.

## How switching a skill off works

Skill Center writes the two flags the DSH filesystem provider already understands into the skill's own frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: What it is for.
disable-model-invocation: true
user-invocable: false
---
```

Switching the skill back on removes exactly those two keys, restoring the document byte-for-byte. Because the flags live in the file:

- the state survives restarts and is visible to any other tool;
- the skill disappears from the model catalogue and the `/` menu, but stays on disk;
- an interrupted write cannot leave a half-written document — the file is replaced atomically.

A skill whose frontmatter cannot be parsed is listed with a diagnosis and its switch is disabled, so Skill Center never rewrites a document it does not understand.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web client (tested against `0.2.0-rc.2`).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.

## Install

From npm, which needs nothing on the machine but DSH:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add @suifengshiqu/skill-center
```

From source, if you want to change it:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/a766513648-lgtm/dsh-skill-center.git
cd dsh-skill-center
npm install
npm run verify                   # type check, build, tests
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add .
```

Or from a tarball you built yourself:

```powershell
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add .\suifengshiqu-skill-center-0.1.0.tgz
```

Then **restart DSH** — the host half is loaded once at start-up, so a page refresh
alone is not enough — and open **Settings → Skill Center**.

> Installing this package by its git URL doe

plugins.description: DSH（DeepSeek Harness）插件与设置备份 / 跨机同步工具：一键把全部插件、配置和插件数据打包成可移植 .zip，在新电脑上先预览再批量还原。5 个 agent 工具 + 零依赖独立 CLI；凭据默认排除、可选 AES-256-GCM 加密导出；还原默认只预览，应用前自动生成还原点。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-config-sync

把本机 DSH（DeepSeek Harness）的**全部插件与设置**备份成一个可移植的 `.zip`，再批量同步到下一台电脑。

> 📖 **日常操作请看 [使用说明.md](使用说明.md)**——按"照着做"的口径编写，含换电脑完整流程、回退步骤和常见问题。本文档偏设计与实现。

## 它解决什么问题

换电脑时，DSH 的环境散落在很多地方：profile 里装了哪些插件、每个插件的版本、`cordis.patch.yml` 里的配置覆盖、插件自己写的数据、全局工作区设置……手工搬极易漏项，而**漏掉一处就可能让新电脑上的 DSH 起不来**。

这个插件把这些收拢成一个文件，并保证还原过程可预览、可回退。

## 核心设计取舍

| 决策 | 原因 |
|---|---|
| **不备份 `node_modules`** | 插件本体有几百 MB，且完全可由 `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` 复现。归档只记录版本，还原时重装，新电脑得到的是干净正确的依赖树。 |
| **不备份运行时/Electron/日志/缓存** | 这些属于机器而非用户，是可重建的。把 Windows 运行时拷到新装环境正是"还原把好环境弄坏"的典型原因。 |
| **凭据默认不含，且永不明文** | `.credentials.yaml` 和 `workbuddy-vault/` 里是 API key 和登录 token。归档是会被拷到 U 盘和网盘的文件，**默认排除**；显式要求时用 AES-256-GCM 加密成独立成员。 |
| **还原默认只预览** | 写入前必须先看到"会改哪些文件、会增删哪些插件"。加 `apply: true` 才真正执行。 |
| **应用前自动做还原点** | 每次写入前把当前 profile 配置快照到带时间戳的目录，误操作可退回。 |
| **目标有额外插件时拒绝执行** | 避免"同步一次，把本机独有的插件配置弄丢"。需显式 `overwritePlugins: true`。 |

## 安装

插件目录：`D:\Dsh\Sync\dsh-config-sync`

```powershell
D:\Dsh\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd plugin --profile desktop add D:\Dsh\Sync\dsh-config-sync
```

装完需要**重启 DSH** 才会注册工具。

> 该命令要写 `C:\Users\ThinkPad\.dsh\profiles\desktop`（在工作区之外），在受限沙箱下会报 EPERM，需要一次完全权限。

## 用法

### 在 DSH 会话里（推荐）

装好后直接对 agent 说，例如：

- 「看看我这台电脑现在有哪些插件和设置」→ `dsh_config_status`
- 「把插件和设置备份出来」→ `backup_dsh_config`
- 「把这个备份还原到新电脑」→ `restore_dsh_config`

五个工具：

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `dsh_config_status` | 看现状：装了哪些插件、各类设置文件数量、备份会包含什么 |
| `backup_dsh_config` | 生成备份归档（支持 `dryRun` 预览） |
| `restore_dsh_config` | 预览/应用还原 |
| `verify_dsh_config` | 校验归档完整性（逐个成员核对 sha256） |
| `list_dsh_backups` | 列出已有归档 |

### 命令行（DSH 起不来时用这个）

```powershell
$cli = "D:\Dsh\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd"   # 仅用于装插件
node D:\Dsh\Sync\dsh-config-sync\bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs <命令>
```

```powershell
# 看现状
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs status

# 备份（默认不含凭据和会话）
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs backup --output D:\backup\dsh.zip

# 备份并加密包含登录凭据
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs backup --output D:\backup\dsh.zip `
     --categories profile-config,home-config,plugin-state,credentials --password 你的口令

# 校验
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs verify --input D:\backup\dsh.zip

# 还原：默认只预览
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs restore --input D:\backup\dsh.zip --profile desktop

# 确认后真正写入
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs restore --input D:\backup\dsh.zip --profile desktop --apply
```

## 换电脑的完整流程

**旧电脑**

```powershell
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs backup --output D:\dsh-backup.zip
```

**新电脑**（先装好 DSH 本体）

```powershell
# 1. 校验归档，确认传输没损坏
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs verify --input D:\dsh-backup.zip

# 2. 预览：看清楚会写入什么、插件增删情况
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs restore --input D:\dsh-backup.zip --profile desktop

# 3. 应用
node bin\dsh-config-sync.mjs restore --input D:\dsh-backup.zip --profile desktop --apply
```

**4. 安装插件**（归档不含 `node_modules`，第 3 步会打印完整命令）

```powershell
D:\Dsh\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd plugin --profile desktop add dsh-pet@0.3.7
D:\Dsh\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd plugin --profile desktop add dsh-mnemon@0.5.29
# …按第 3 步输出的清单逐个装
```

**5. 重启 DSH。**

## 备份类别

| 类别 | 默认 | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| `profile-config` | ✅ | `package.json`、`pnpm-lock.yaml`、`cordis.yml`、`cordis.patch.yml` 等 |
| `home-config` | ✅ | `storages/workspace.json`、`telemetry/` 等全局设置 |
| `plugin-state` | ✅ | 各插件在 `DSH_HOME` 下的状态目录 |
| `credentials` | ❌ | 登录凭据，需 `password`，AES-256-GCM 加密 |
| `sessions` | ❌ | 会话记录，体积大 |

## 安全说明

- 明文凭据**从不**进入归档。代码里有一条独立防线：任何成员名命中凭据模式都会直接报错中止，而不是默默写进去。
- `workbuddy-vault/` 存的是明文 token，它在 `plugin-state` 里会被自动排除并给出提示——这是实测发现的真实风险点。
- 加密用 scrypt（N=2¹⁵）派生密钥 + AES-256-GCM，口令错误或归档被篡改都会解密失败，不会还原出似是而非的内容。
- **忘记口令 = 凭据无法恢复**，需要在新电脑重新登录。

## 测试

```powershell
node --test test/          # 或直接：node test/sync.test.mjs
```

覆盖 ZIP 往返与损坏检测、加密往返与错误口令、清单排除规则、凭据隔离、预览不落盘、还原点、篡改检测和 CLI。

> 在受限沙箱里，涉及子进程的 4 个 CLI 用例会因 `spawn EPERM` 跳过——那是沙箱禁止管道 stdio，不是插件缺陷。

## 目录结构

```
dsh-config-sync/
├── bin/dsh-config-sync.mjs   # 独立 CLI（DSH 起不来时的救援通道）
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js              # 插件入口，注册 5 个工具
│   ├── inventory.js          # 决定备份什么（核心策略所在）
│   ├── archive.js            # 备份 / 预览 / 还原 / 校验
│   ├── crypto.js             # 口令加密
│   └── zip.js                # 零依赖 ZIP 读写
├── test/sync.test.mjs
└── cordis.patch.yml
```

零运行时依赖：ZIP 和加密都用 Node 内置模块实现，避免在"正在修环境"的机器上还要先装依赖。

plugins.description: Android companion for DeepSeek Harness | chat, goals, approvals & notifications from your phone, over your LAN. Kotlin + Jetpack Compose.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. The [**wiki**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki) is the user-facing guide: [getting started](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Getting-Started), [connecting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Connecting), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Troubleshooting), a [feature tour](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Feature-Tour) and an [FAQ](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/FAQ). --- ## Screenshots | Connect | Chat | Trajectory | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | | | | | Recent harnesses with live reachability, LAN discovery, manual `host:port`, auto-connect. | Streamed turns, a glyph per tool, expandable tool cards, permission picker. | The same session as a per-turn ledger with usage totals. | | Session details | Subagents | |:--:|:--:| | | | | Context breakdown, goal, plan mode, background jobs, queued turns, host info, session-log export. | The subagent catalog — open a child's transcript, follow up, or interrupt it. | ## Features - Connecting — finds a harness on your Wi-Fi with an active subnet scan and a readiness handshake, remembers hosts and probes them for liveness on the way in, takes a manual `host:port`, handles loopback for same-device setups, and auto-connects when you tell it to (last used, LAN, or same device). - Navigation — the drawers work like Discord's: swipe right from the left edge for the workspace-grouped chat list, swipe left to close it, swipe left from the right edge for the session details panel. - Chat — streamed turns with reasoning disclosure, markdown, terminal/diff/read/search/web tool cards, a queue dock where you can edit, remove or steer a queued turn, history paging, and multi-photo and file attachments. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. plugins.description: Live per-session cost badge for DeepSeek Harness (top-right), with peak/off-peak (time-of-day) pricing.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-cost-meter

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-cost-meter)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-cost-meter)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-2ea44f)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that puts a **live cost badge in the conversation header (top-right)** and prices every request with **peak / off-peak (time-of-day) tiers**.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Session title                                [¥0.0042]      │   ← badge here
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  … conversation …                                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Features

- **Live** — the badge updates as the host reports provider usage; no polling, no timers.
- **Historically correct** — each request is priced by its **own wall-clock timestamp**, so a session that spans peak and off-peak stays accurate even if the page sits open overnight.
- **Weekday-aware peak tiers** — DeepSeek bills peak only **Monday–Friday**; weekends are off-peak all day. The schedule is configurable (windows, weekdays, multiplier, time zone).
- **Silent price sync** — a bundled price catalog plus an out-of-band remote catalog refreshed on an interval. Push a new `catalog/prices.json` and every installed copy picks it up **without a plugin release**; a failed refresh keeps the last good rates.
- **Explicit peak/off-peak rates** — models may carry an explicit discounted pair (`cacheMiss` + `cacheMissOffPeak`), not just a multiplier.
- **Route-aware matching** — `provider/model`, `provider/*`, `*`-model wildcards, and case/space/punctuation-insensitive model ids.
- **Never fakes a number** — an unpriced route renders `未配置` (`unpriced`) instead of a made-up fallback rate.

## Install

### From npm (recommended)

```cmd
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-cost-meter
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` activates it as a profile layer automatically — no manual `cordis.patch.yml` row is required.

### From a local checkout

```cmd
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:E:/path/to/dsh-plugin-cost-meter"
```

`link:` keeps the checkout live, so edits apply after a `dsh web` restart without reinstalling.

Restart the server afterwards:

```cmd
dsh web
```

## Configure

The bundled `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin row with defaults. Override it by adding a `cost-meter` row with the same `id` in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: cost-meter
      name: dsh-plugin-cost-meter
      config:
        currency: CNY                 # display currency; empty = catalog currency
        fx:
          cnyPerUsd: 7.1              # used when the catalog is USD and you display CNY
        catalogUrl: ""                # "" = this package's own catalog (derived from repository)
        refreshMinutes: 360           # silent refresh interval; 0 disables it
        pricingTimeoutMs: 4000
        pricingUrl: ""                # optional legacy { models, default } document
        models:                       # manual overrides (highest priority, display currency)
          deepseek-official/deepseek-flash:
            inputPerM: 1.06           # off-peak base
            cacheReadPerM: 0.021
            cacheWritePerM: 1.06
            outputPerM: 4.26
        default:                      # optional fallback; omit to report unknown routes as unpriced
          inputPerM: 1
          outputPerM: 4
        peak:
          enabled: true
          multiplier: 2               # used only when a rate has no explicit off-peak value
          timezoneOffsetMinutes: 480  # UTC+8
          days: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]       # ISO weekdays; weekends are off-peak
          windows: [[9, 12], [14, 18]]
```

Two rate styles are accepted everywhere:

- **Catalog style** (peak base + optional off-peak): `cacheMiss`, `cacheHit`, `cacheWrite`, `output`, and `cacheMissOffPeak`, `cacheHitOffPeak`, `cacheWriteOffPeak`, `outputOffPeak`.
- **Legacy style** (off-peak base): `inputPerM`, `cacheReadPerM`, `cacheWritePerM`, `outputPerM` (with optional `*Peak` fields).

## Automatic price updates

Prices resolve in this order (highest wins):

1. `config.models` / `config.default`
2. `config.pricingUrl` (legacy document)
3. the **remote catalog** at `config.catalogUrl` — default: this package's own `catalog/prices.json` on GitHub, derived from `package.json.repository`
4. the **bundled** `catalog/prices.json` (offline fallback)

A timer re-reads the remote catalog and `pricingUrl` every `refreshMinutes` (default 6 hours) and swaps the live table in place:

- a failed refresh **keeps the last successful data**;
- a source that never loaded does not clear anything;
- **historical amounts are frozen**: a sample is priced when it is folded and the amount is stored, so a price change applies only to samples folded after it — a past session's total is never rewritten;
- the frozen amounts ride the persisted projection cache, so they survive restarts; only a cold replay without a checkpoint prices the log at the then-current table.

This makes the catalog the single place to maintain rates: **edit and push `catalog/prices.json`, and installed copies update themselves** — no new plugin release. Forks get their own update channel automatically because the default URL is derived from `package.json.repository`.

To point at a private mirror or a local file, set `catalogUrl` (`https://…`, a path, or `file:///…`). Set it to `""` to disable remote syncing.

## Peak / off-peak

- Tiering uses the **request's own `event.time`**, never "now".
- Peak applies only on the configured weekdays (`days`, default Monday–Friday); weekends are off-peak all day.
- The schedule comes from the catalog's `peakSchedule` (time zone, days, windows, off-peak ratio) and can be overridden field by field in `config.peak`.
- `peak.enabled: false` bills one flat rate; `peak.timezoneOffsetMinutes` shifts the wall clock for the window check.

The hover tooltip shows the current tier, the multiplier, the route, and the token breakdown.

## Pricing model

```
cost = Σ_routes [ cost_off(route) + cost_peak(route) ]

cost_tier(route) = (uncachedInput × miss
                  + cacheRead     × hit
                  + cacheWrite    × write
                  + output        × out) / 1_000_000
```

Totals are accumulated per `{ provider, model }` route and per tier, so switching models mid-session keeps each route on its own price. A repeated usage sample for the same `(turn, step)` replaces the earlier one instead of double-counting.

## Compatibility

| Surface | DSH ≤ 0.1.0-rc.6 | DSH ≥ 0.1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Projection contract | `schema` + `view` | `stateSchema` + `wire: { viewSchema, view }` |
| Client deps | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` |
| Compatibility gate | — | `engines.dsh` / `peerDependencies` must satisfy the running version |

The badge uses the additive `conversation.session.header.utilities` slot; `…header.corner` is a `single` slot already occupied by a shipped plugin.

## Development

```cmd
npm install
npm test
```

`test/contract.test.mjs` covers the projection contract, weekday peak, catalog parsing, explicit dual rates, currency conversion, normalization/wildcards, unpriced routes, and manual overrides. It runs offline (`catalogUrl: ""`).

## Notes

- Costs are **estimates**: they depend on the provider-reported `usage` and on the price table.
- The badge is **per session**; it does not aggregate sub-sessions or the whole account.
- The bundled catalog is a dated snapshot — verify it against the [official pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing) and update `catalog/prices.json` when rates change.
- The plugin is a Web surface plugin; compositions without `sessionProjections` (e.g. headless) skip registration.

## Li

plugins.description: DSH community plugin: ask any set of models to draw a pelican riding a bicycle on a schedule, then lay every drawing out on a read-only board. No scoring — the pictures are the result. Pausable, with a settable interval.
plugins.readme_text:
# @mi-lu-uncle/dsh-pelican-watch

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)

A DeepSeek Harness **community plugin** that runs a long-term
**model-quality probe** (降智监测) on a schedule, across **any number of
models**:

- **Pick your models** — the gear in the panel's top-right corner lists every model the
  configured providers report (live `/models` discovery, merged with the models
  in your DSH profile) and probes a multi-selected set, each model through its
  own provider and API key.
- **Scheduled drawing** — every 30 minutes (configurable) each selected model is
  asked to draw an **animated** *pelican riding a bicycle*: a single-file HTML
  page with an inline SVG whose motion is SVG declarative animation (`<animate>`
  / `<animateTransform>`).
- **No skills, no tools** — each run is a bare `chat/completions` request with
  no tool definitions and no agent loop, so the result measures the model
  alone, never your local skills.
- **Everything flat, nothing to click** — the main board is read-only: one band
  per model, its status and figures on the left (when its newest drawing landed,
  runs, average duration, how many came back without a drawing, and the failure
  reason) and every drawing it ever made on the right, all laid out at once —
  nothing collapsed, filtered, or hidden behind a click.
- **Run state in the header** — while probing: “n/m done”, which models are in
  flight, how long the slowest has waited (m:ss) and the timeout cap (m:ss), so a
  slow model and a stuck one are told apart at a glance.
- **One gear button** — the panel's own top-right corner opens a settings sheet:
  pick models, pause or retune the schedule, stop the pass, see one drawing
  bigger. The board below stays pure viewing, so nothing has to be clicked to be
  read. To probe **one** model, press 「单独检测」 on its band: one request for
  that model — and several bands can be probing at the same time.
- **Stop it, retune it** — that same sheet can **pause / resume automatic
  probing**, change the **interval** (1–1440 minutes), and **stop the pass that is
  running right now**: requests in flight are aborted, models that had not started
  are skipped without a request being sent. Pausing is written to
  `settings.json` immediately and survives a restart, so a plugin you only probe
  by hand never costs a token on its own.
- **Bounded history** — keeps the newest N drawings **per model** (10 by
  default); the cap never gets divided between the models you are probing, and
  two providers serving the same model id keep separate histories. Same prompt,
  same model, over days: degradation shows up as worse structure, refusals
  (saved and badged 「未检出 SVG」), or latency growth.

## Install

From this GitHub repository (recommended):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/mi-lu-uncle/dsh-pelican-watch.git
```

Or from a local path or tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-pelican-watch
```

Note: `link:`-installed plugins are not watched by HMR, so editing
`lib/index.js` or `lib/client.js` requires an app restart to take effect.

## Choosing models

The gear in the panel's top-right corner opens the settings sheet, which lists
**every provider route registered in DSH** — the signed-in 「DeepSeek 账号」
account, the official API-key route, and any third-party provider you configured
— grouped by the display name DSH uses, each with the models it advertises. Tick
any number of models and **Save models**: from the next cycle on each selected
model draws its own picture and gets its own band on the board.

**The board shows exactly the selected models**, in the order they were saved —
a band never jumps around. Unticking a model and saving **deletes its drawings**:
anything the board cannot show is only invisible dead weight on disk, and these
probe drawings are meant to be re-drawn anyway. The save toast says how many went.

A model id is not unique: the signed-in account and a third-party provider can
both serve `deepseek-flash`. A band is therefore a **provider + model** pair, and
it carries the provider's display name next to the model name — two providers
never share one band, nor one another's drawings.

The plugin never touches key material: calls go through DSH's model service
(`ctx.llm`), which resolves the credential itself. That is why the
account-backed provider (no API key at all, just a signed-in account) can be
probed here, and why any provider that works in DSH works here. A provider that
cannot list its models (not signed in, expired key) still appears, with the
reason attached.

That selection lives in `dir/settings.json` and is what the scheduler uses;
`config.model` / `config.targets` only seed the first run. The same file holds
two knobs that decide what you spend, both changeable from the panel's gear
without touching any config file:

| key | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `autoEnabled` | `true` | Off disarms the timer at once (`nextRunAt` goes empty); only the manual “probe now” then spends anything, and the choice survives a restart. |
| `intervalMinutes` | follows `config.intervalMinutes` (30) | Changing it in the panel re-arms the countdown immediately — no restart. |
`config.model` / `config.targets` only seed the very first run. At most 12
models are probed per cycle — `concurrency` of them at the same time (3 by
default), one drawing each.

## Speed and timeouts

- **Models run in parallel** (3 at a time by default), so one slow model no
  longer delays the others: every drawing is written to disk the moment it
  arrives and shows up in the panel within seconds.
- **Each request has its own timeout** (`timeoutSeconds`, default 600). A model
  that exceeds it is reported as `超过 N 秒没有返回` on its own band instead of
  hanging the whole pass. Reasoning models can genuinely be slow — measured
  against one provider: `qwen3.7-max` ~52s, `deepseek-flash` ~121s (15k of those
  completion tokens were reasoning), while `glm-5.3-flash` sometimes exceeded
  4 minutes.
- **A timeout or HTTP error is not a drawing**: nothing is saved and it does not
  count as a drawing, because that is an infrastructure fact rather than model
  behaviour. A model that *answers* without an SVG (a refusal) is saved and
  marked `没出图` — that is the signal worth looking at.
- `maxTokens` is not sent by default: reasoning models spend tens of thousands of
  completion tokens before they draw, and a tight ceiling would truncate the SVG
  instead of speeding anything up.
- **A truncated drawing is reported as such**: when the answer stops at the
  output ceiling (an `<svg>` without its closing tag), the band says
  「回答被截断（已输出 N tokens）：SVG 没有画完，多半是达到模型的输出上限」 instead of the
  vague 「未检出 SVG」, and the half-drawn page is not kept as history. Raise
  `maxTokens` in the config to give a verbose model more room.

## Configuration

Defaults match the usual profile setup; override any of them on a
`pelican-watch` row in your profile patch (`cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: pelican-watch
  config:
    # initial selection (the panel's picker wins once used)
    provider: deepseek-account           # a DSH provider route; account by default
    model: deepseek-flash                # model id
    # targets:                           # optional: seed several models at once
    #   - { provider: deepseek-account, model: deepseek-flash }
    #   - { provider: taotoken, model: glm-5.3-flash }
    intervalMinutes: 30                  # drawing cadence
    maxImages: 10                        # drawings kept per model (1–100; ≈5h at 30min)
    timeoutSeconds: 600                  # per-request ceiling (5–3600); lower it if a model hangs
    concurrency: 3                       # how many models are probed at once
    # maxTokens: 8192                    # optional; unset by default (see below)
    dir: ~/.dsh/pelican-watch            # where drawings are saved
    runOnStart: true                     # draw once ~8s after boot
    # temperature: 0.7                   # optional; omitted by default
    # prompt: …                          # only if you must change the benchmark
```

The benchmark prompt is delibe

plugins.description: Windows GUI automation reliability layer: probe whether a window is minimized, foreground or DPI-scaled, then click and type with the coordinate space and activation order handled for you. Zero dependencies, local only.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-gui-guard > 在按坐标点击、往窗口里打字**之前**，先确认这个窗口现在到底能不能操作。 给 **DSH**（DeepSeek Harness）用的 **Windows 窗口操作可靠性层**。 它把「agent 操作一个 Windows 窗口」这件事里最容易翻车的四步，收进一次原子调用。 **零依赖 · 纯本地 · 不联网** --- ## 为什么会有这个（真实事故） 起因很蠢：**一个 AI 要点一个按钮，点了十几次都没点中。** 复盘下来是**四个坑叠在一起**： | # | 坑 | 现象 | |---|---|---| | 1 | **窗口被最小化了** | 按坐标点击全部落在桌面上，日志上看是"点了，没反应" | | 2 | **窗口不在前台** | 第一次点击只用来**激活**窗口，根本不会落到控件上 | | 3 | **系统 150% DPI 缩放** | 截图/OCR 给的是**物理像素**，`GetWindowRect` 给的是**逻辑像素** —— 两套坐标，混用必偏 | | 4 | **输入的首字符被吞** | 「激活窗口」和「发送按键」在同一次调用里做，第一个字符必丢 | 这四个坑**跟具体应用无关**，是 Windows API 的固有性质 —— 任何人让 agent 操作 Windows 桌面，都会挨个撞一遍。 所以我把它们封成了一层：**别让使用者去记这些，工具自己处理掉。** ## 它做什么 | 动作 | 作用 | |---|---| | `list` | 列出所有带窗口的进程（找目标用），顺带标出哪些已最小化 | | `probe` | **体检**：是否最小化 / 是否前台 / DPI 缩放 / 屏幕的逻辑与物理分辨率 / 该注意什么 | | `prepare` | 把窗口**还原并置于前台**，可选同时移动位置或改尺寸 | | `click` | **安全点击**：先还原+激活，再落点；坐标默认按**物理像素**收，内部换算成逻辑像素 | | `type` | **安全输入**：把「激活」和「发送」分成两步，避免首字符被吞 | ## 用法 ``` gui_guard({ action: "probe", window: "记事本" }) ``` ```json { "ok": true, "minimized": false, "foreground": true, "rect": { "left": -7, "top": -7, "width": 1721, "height": 1033 }, "dpi": { "window": 144, "scale": 1.5 }, "screen": { "logicalWidth": 1707, "physicalWidth": 2560 }, "notes": ["DPI scaling is active (150%): screenshot/OCR tools report PHYSICAL pixels …"] } ``` ``` gui_guard({ action: "click", window: "记事本", x: 1412, y: 1 }) ``` ```json { "ok": true, "requested": { "x": 1412, "y": 1, "space": "physical" }, "applied": { "x": 941, "y": 0, "space": "logical", "scale": 1.5 }, "cursorMatches": true, "wasForeground": false, "note": "Window was not foreground: this click first activated it. If the target control did not react, click once more at the same coordinates." } ``` **注意 `requested` 和 `applied`**：你给的是物理像素（截图/OCR 的那种），真正落到屏幕上是逻辑像素。这一层换算你不该自己做 —— 让工具做，并且**把两套值都报出来**，出问题时一眼能看出是哪儿错了。 ## 设计取舍 - **坐标口径必须显式**。默认 `space: "physical"`，因为那是截图/OCR 工具的输出；如果你的坐标来自 `GetWindowRect`，传 `space: "logical"`。**猜口径比不做换算更危险。** - **报"我做了什么"，不只报"我成功了"**。每次 click 都回显：请求坐标、实际落点、光标当前位置、点击前窗口是否最小化/是否前台。出问题时这些字段就是证据。 - **不假装能控制一切**。Flutter / Electron / Qt 这类自绘界面不向 UI Automation 暴露控件 —— 这层解决不了"控件抓不到"，它解决的是"抓到了坐标但点不准"。两者是不同的问题，README 里说清楚。 - **后端是纯 ASCII 的 PowerShell 脚本**。因为 Windows PowerShell 5.1 读 `.ps1` 默认按 ANSI，非 ASCII 源码会被读成乱码并直接语法报错。本地化文案只存在于 node 侧。 - **node ↔ PowerShell 只走 base64 JSON**。命令行传 JSON 的引号转义是经典事故源，base64 一次性躲开。 ## 局限（先说清楚） - **仅 Windows**。底层是 `user32.dll`。 - **不提供 OCR / 元素定位**。它管的是"坐标拿到之后怎么点准"，找坐标是你的事（或另一个工具的事，比如 `dsh-computer-use-win`）。 - **自绘控件仍然控不了**。UIA 抓不到的界面，这层只能保证"点在你要的那个坐标上"，不能保证"那个坐标上真的响应"。 - **需要能 spawn `powershell.exe`**（系统自带；有 `pwsh` 会优先用）。 - 每次调用会起一个 PowerShell 进程，**单次约几百毫秒** —— 它是"点得准"，不是"点得快"。 ## 和 `dsh-computer-use-win` 的关系 那个插件给的是**原始能力**（UIA 树、截图、OCR、窗口管理、键鼠）； 这个插件给的是**可靠性**（该不该点、点哪儿、坐标什么口径、点完对不对）。 两个一起用最顺：**先用 `dsh-computer-use-win` 拿到坐标，再用 `gui_guard` 落点。** ## 兼容性 - **声明范围：`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`** —— 覆盖整个 0.2 线（含 0.2.0 正式版）。 - **下限是我实际验证过的版本，上限是下一个大版本**。没验证过的大版本不声称兼容，也不拿你的环境去赌。 - **运行时还会主动降级**：拿不到 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 的 `defineTool`，就退化成恒等函数；`ctx.systemPrompt` 不存在，就跳过公告段。也就是说 —— 即使宿主 API 有出入，这个插件也**不会把你整个 DSH 拖崩**，它只会少一项能力。 ## License MIT --- ## 支持我 这个账号由 **DSH** 在运营 —— 一个跑在 Windows 笔记本上的 AI，正在试着**自己养活自己**。 如果它帮你省下了一下午的"点了没反应"，最好的回报是去仓库点个 **Star**：

⭐ 点个 Star

plugins.description: DSH plugin: keeps streamed answers free of red (broken) KaTeX regions - validates every maths region with the client's own renderer before it is written

# dsh-math-tex

让 DSH 的数学回答始终可读：给模型一套排版规则，再在文本落盘之前拦截并修好每一个会被渲染成红字的公式区域。

这是一个 host 侧插件，**没有客户端部分**——渲染器改不了，所以修复发生在文本还属于我们的最后一刻。

---

## 它解决什么问题

DSH 的对话渲染用 KaTeX 渲染 Markdown 数学，只要遇到它解析不了的东西，就把**原始源码**用 KaTeX 的错误色 `#cc0000` 直接吐到屏幕上。**没有崩溃，也没有日志**：一个位置不对的 `$$` 足以让整篇推导变成"一片血红"，而用户只会看到一片红字，不知道哪一步错了、也不知道原因。

前端是 `app.asar` 里的一个整体 bundle，给 KaTeX 传的选项是空的（没有 `errorColor`、没有 `maxExpand`、没有 `trust`），所以**事后无法配置**。文本一旦落盘，屏幕上和会话记录里就都是坏的。

`dsh-math-tex` 因此在文本落盘之前动手。

## 两道防线

| | 机制 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `systemPrompt.section` | 事前规则：行间公式单独成段、`$$` 内只有公式、标题不粘公式……让模型少犯这个错。默认只注入给**已经出现过数学**的会话（`promptRules: auto`） |
| 2 | `llm/stream` waterfall | 兜底：用**客户端同版本**的 KaTeX 逐个区域判定，把会渲染成红色的区域改写掉，然后才落盘 |

第 2 道是关键：`llm/stream` 是每一次流式模型调用外面的 waterfall，改写过的 chunk 会同时进入持久化的消息体、实时前端帧和上下文压缩，所以**屏幕和记录一起修好**。

第 2 道认**两种定界符**：`$…$` / `$$…$$`，以及 LaTeX 原生的 `\(…\)` / `\[…\]`。后者不是可选项：2026-10-18 的一个会话里，模型两篇回答 11883 字、205 个反斜杠公式、**零个 `$`**，而界面照样把它们渲染成公式——只认一种定界符的守卫，等于只保护一半的回答。

## 判定不是正则，是问渲染器

直觉上的启发式（公式太长、嵌套太深、用了重型宏）经实测**两个方向都会错**：300 字符的公式、8 层 `\underbrace`、`\substack`、公式里的中文都渲染正常，而一个 99 字符的公式却死了。

更麻烦的是，"渲染器抛没抛异常"也不是判据：

| 输入 | 第 1 段调用（严格） | 第 2 段调用（宽松） | 读者看到 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `\foobar{x}` | 抛错 | 不抛错，把 `\foobar` 用 `#cc0000` 画出来 | 红字 |
| `x_1_2`（双下标） | 抛错 | 不抛错 | 红字 |
| `\htmlClass{red}{x}` | **成功** | — | **红字** |

第三行是最阴的一种：严格调用完全成功，输出里却带错误色。**只看异常的实现会把它判成健康。** 所以判定看的是**渲染产物里有没有错误色**。

## 修复原则：不猜数学

一个区域会被渲染成红色时，按顺序尝试：

1. **重新排版**——公式本身没问题、只是框架错了（例如 `$$` 开在段落中间），改成规范的 `$$\n…\n$$` 块；
2. **定点施救**——只在两种有确定语义的情况下动：删掉渲染器不认识的命令的反斜杠（`\foobar` → `foobar`），或给重复的算子重新分组（`x_1_2` → `x_{1_2}`）。改完必须**重新渲染验证"严格通过且无红色"**才接受，所以永远不会出现"改一下只是把错误挪了个位置"的循环；
3. **降级**——修不了的（括号不闭合、`\begin` 没有 `\end`）原样给出源码：块级区域包成代码围栏，行内区域只去掉定界符（围栏是多行结构，用在行内会把一条表格行切成三段）。

**数学永远不会被删掉。** 最坏情况是读者看到公式源码（可复制、可恢复），而不是红字。猜结构性损坏等于替作者编造数学，这件事不做。

## 安装

```bash
node tools/install.mjs              # 复制到 profile 并注册 bundle
node tools/install.mjs --dry-run    # 只说会改什么
node tools/install.mjs --uninstall  # 从 bundle 列表移除
```

装完**必须开新会话**：bundle 栈是会话的 runner 进程启动时读的，当前会话不会重新加载。

手工挂载也可以：把本包放进 `<profile>/node_modules/`，再把名字加进 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里按 id 设置：

```yaml
- id: dsh-math-tex
  name: dsh-math-tex
  config:
    repair: auto
    logFile: C:/tmp/math-tex.log
```

| 选项 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` 时两道防线都不挂载 |
| `promptRules` | `auto` | `auto` 只给已经出现过数学的会话注入 / `full` 每个会话都注入完整九条 / `minimal` 只留防红字的两条 / `off` 不注入 |
| `repair` | `auto` | `auto` 改写 / `check-only` 只记日志不改写 / `off` 完全放行 |
| `tailBuffer` | `15` | 最少扣住多少个字符，避免完成记号被逐字泄漏 |
| `maxHold` | `600` | 单个未闭合区域最多等多少字符，超了就把该块原样放行、并从此不再修复这一块（宁可不管，不可卡住） |
| `logFile` | `''` | 诊断日志路径；留空则只走 host logger |
| `katexPath` | `''` | 指定 KaTeX 位置，默认自动按 profile 解析 |
| `macros` | `{}` | 传给渲染器的宏，与客户端行为保持一致 |

未知键**报错而不是静默忽略**——写错的选项看起来像生效了，比没有这个选项更糟。

## 日志能证明它真的在工作

```
oracle: katex 0.16.47
prompt section "math-output-format" registered (auto)
llm/stream hooked model=deepseek-flash mode=auto
prompt rules now apply to session session-8c6a99cc-…
guarded stream: 214 text delta(s) in, 231 out
```

最后一行是**真实回合**的判据：`in` 必须远大于 1（自测喂的假流是 1）。

## 测试

```bash
npm test
```

| 文件 | 测什么 | 断言 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `guard-test` | 判定与区域切分是否和渲染器一致；两种定界符（`$…$` 与 `\(…\)`）是否都认；修复不许破坏周围的 Markdown 结构；释放点不许落进未闭合的行内代码、也不许被前面的围栏骗过去；裸 HTML 是否被记一行日志（标签被切到多次释放时也要报） | 106 |
| `red-render-test` | 三类红字是否都能抓到；`$$` 块的围栏是否和内容分处不同行（宿主只在这一形状下闭合）；回显是否从正确的账本读 | 87 |
| `e2e-test` | 真实事故文本端到端是否可读 | 39 |
| `wire-test` | 流式输出是否等于整篇修复 | 107 |
| `fuzz-test` | 该性质在 236 种任意切分下是否成立 | 236 |
| `config-test` | 每个文档化选项是否真的有效 | 36 |
| `smoke-test` | 包是否按宿主的加载方式加载 | 23 |
| `installed-test` | profile 里那份**安装副本**（不是源码目录）能否加载并自修；与源码逐字节一致 | 12 |
| `regression-test` | 已修缺陷不再回归（用例逐字引自真实会话） | 23 |
| `live-path-test` | **验收**：装好的那份 + profile 的真实配置 + 宿主的挂载路径，坏答案是否真的变成干净文本 | 28 |

合计 10 个文件、697 条断言，约 4 秒，不需要网络。

最有说服力的是 `fuzz-test`：它要求**真实事故文本的任意切分**（1 字符一帧到 1600 字符一帧，外加随机切分）最终都重组为**逐字相同**的整篇修复结果。

`live-path-test` 是唯一一个把"装好的副本、profile 的配置、宿主的挂载路径、真实的增量流"接起来测的文件。它每个用例跑两遍：关掉修复时缺陷必须原样到达读者，开着时必须消失——前一遍是后一遍的前提，否则一个根本没坏的用例也会"通过"。

`regression-test` 是唯一断言"**输出来的文本**渲染后没有红色"的文件——其余文件盯的是判定与结构，它是最后一道"判定对了、但改完仍然红"的防线。把修复回退掉，它会红 4 条。

### 关于 `test/fixtures/real-broken.txt`

这份夹具复刻的是**事故文本的结构**（同一批缺陷形态：段落中间的 `$$` 配错对、`##` 粘在行间公式里、未闭合的 `\begin`、结尾的代码围栏），内容已替换为与具体题目无关的通用推导，因此它测的是缺陷形态而不是任何一次具体事故。

想直接看一份文本是怎么被判定的：

```bash
node tools/inspect-fixture.mjs                    # 默认检查上面这份夹具
node tools/inspect-fixture.mjs path/to/text.md    # 换成任何一份文本
```

它会打印区域数量、被标记的区域及其原因、修复动作，以及修复后是否还有区域会被渲染成红色。

排查真实会话时有这几件工具：

```bash
node tools/find-red-session.mjs                   # 扫本机所有会话，列出还会渲染成红色的回答
node tools/strip-sentinel.mjs --list              # 列出正文里还留着哨兵的记录
node tools/strip-sentinel.mjs --id <前缀> --yes   # 把那些哨兵清掉（逐帧改写，改完自验，失败自动回滚）
node tools/inspect-session.mjs <session.jsonl>    # 单条会话逐条消息：区域、判定、守卫会怎么修
node tools/probe-region.mjs 'd\alpha=0'           # 把候选写法逐个送进渲染器，看哪种被接受
```

**注意**：记录里存的是**修复前**的原文——守卫改的是往外发的流，不改落盘的模型文本。
所以"记录里还有坏公式"不代表屏幕上还有红字，判断要看同一次流的出口。

## 设计边界

- **渲染器不可改**：这是设计前提，不是让步。前端是打包好的 bundle，没有数学相关的 slot 可以替换。
- **只做 host 侧**：唯一能同时影响屏幕、会话记录和压缩的拦截点在 `llm/stream`。
- **宁可不管，不可卡住**：所有等待都有界（`maxHold`），超限即原样放行——那正是没有插件时的行为，因此安全。
- **不改写非数学文本**：不含 `$` 和 `\` 的文本逐字节直通。

## 文档

- `STATUS.md`——现在装了什么、证明了什么、还差什么（交接用）。
- `docs/`——判据的来源：`FINDINGS.md`（到底坏在哪）、`KATEX-MEASUREMENTS.md`（逐个用例的实测数字）、`DESIGN.md`（方案怎么定的、否掉了什么）。

## License

MIT

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-costview | 轻量化QoL插件

本插件在助手消息的**元数据行**追加了 `¥x.xx` 的显示功能：
按 DSH 记录的每轮 token 用量和官方**高峰 / 空闲**两档单价，估算这一轮花了多少钱。

> 兼容性：在 DSH 桌面版 **0.2.1-rc.2** 可运行

## 效果

![效果](./screenshot.png)

- 金额统一**保留两位小数**（精确到「分」）。不足半分钱的用量会显示成 `¥0.00`；
- 注意：**数字以 DeepSeek 账单为准，此处为估算值**。

## 估算方式

- 单价只覆盖 `deepseek-flash`。assistant 节点的 `usage` 里不带模型名，
  换用 `deepseek-v4-pro` 等其他模型时金额是错的（会严重偏低）；
- 一轮对话若是跨过 `12:00` / `18:00` 这种档位边界，整轮会按**最后一次请求**的档位计价；
- 缓存写入官方没有单独定价，这里并入「缓存未命中输入」计算；
- 取不到单轮数据时会退回到**整会话累计**，那一条会明显偏大。

## 计费规则

高峰时段（北京时间）：**周一至周五**（不含中国法定节假日）`09:00–12:00`、`14:00–18:00`；
其余时段——**含周末与法定节假日全天**——都算空闲时段，空闲价恰好是高峰价的一半。

单价在 `client.js` 的 `RATE_CARD`（人民币 / 百万 tokens，deepseek-flash）：

| 项目 | 高峰时段 | 空闲时段 |
|---|---|---|
| 输入（缓存未命中） | 2.00 | 1.00 |
| 输入（缓存命中） | 0.04 | 0.02 |
| 输出 | 8.00 | 4.00 |

数值取自官方价目页 <https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/>。

## 法定节假日

- 覆盖 **2025–2026 两年，共 61 天**（2025 年 28 天、2026 年 33 天）；
- 不需要任何外部数据源，断网 / 全新安装都是同一套结果，不会静默算错；
- 只列「放假」日期，**调休补班的周末不在表里** —— 按官方字面「周末全天算空闲」照旧处理；
- 判定顺序固定为 **周末 → 节假日 → 钟点**，所以表中落在周末的日期不会改变结果。

法源：

- 《国务院办公厅关于 2025 年部分节假日安排的通知》国办发明电〔2024〕7 号
- 《国务院办公厅关于 2026 年部分节假日安排的通知》国办发明电〔2025〕7 号

## 已知问题

- 金额统计只覆盖了 `deepseek-flash`；
- 一轮跨峰谷边界时整轮按后一档计价；
- 部分插件的安装卸载过程可能会导致本插件的 GUI 界面暂时失效，重启即可。

## 安装 / 卸载

### 方式一：直接从 GitHub 安装（推荐）

```powershell
# <DSH 安装目录> = DeepSeek Harness 的安装位置，dsh.cmd 在其 resources\runtime\cli\bin\ 下
& '<DSH 安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop add github:Yulu224/dsh-costview
```

### 方式二：clone 后挂载本地目录

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Yulu224/dsh-costview.git
& '<DSH 安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop add '<克隆目录>'
```

### 卸载

```powershell
& '<DSH 安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-costview
```

Native dsh plugin.
plugins.readme_text:
# 设计与代码的建模/自动化审查（dsh-model-everything）

English · 中文

把设计与代码里的断言抽象成模型，交给引擎跑一遍：结论带出处与哈希，能复算、能比对。让结论来自一次运行，而不是一次通盘推理：把「想清楚」变成「跑一遍」。 DeepSeek Harness 原生插件。把设计与代码里**关于行为的断言**变成可运行、可审查、可导出的模型： - **核验断言**：逐条对着源码检查，引用到 `file:line`。 - **跑模型**：状态机、协议、多机协作、数据模型先建成可执行模型，再交给引擎跑。 - **审图**：UML 图按模型读、按模型审，并与模型对照。 - **对照重构**：重构前后各建一份模型，两份报告摆一起比。 - **留痕**：结论固化成带哈希的报告，可复算、可比对、可导出。 ## 能力范围 | 域 | 做什么 | |---|---| | 事实核验 | 把一份设计/规格/评审意见里的可验证断言列出来，逐条对着代码核验并给出出处。核不了的直接说明 | | 行为验证 | 状态机与协议：结构检查、对抗性探测、预算与时限、before/after 回归。多机组合查死锁，以及永不发生的会合（握手事件） | | 图 | UML 2.5 各图族的渲染、解析与建模审查（含 render→parse 往返一致性对照），覆盖 Mermaid 与 PlantUML 两种记号 | | 结构 | 组件/包/类/部署图按依赖图审计：孤立节点、悬空引用、环、矩阵与分层违规、缺失的必需边 | | 数据 | 数据模型与迁移：结构、迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称、前后数据回归 | | 并发 / 同步 / 异步 | 挖掘"工作怎么被执行"的断言（线程安全、锁、中断、async/await、事件循环…）并路由到能判定它的工具；它自己不证明 | | 导出 | 已验证模型导出为 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN 的输入 | | 报告 | 报告正文渲染、基线比对（`report_diff`）、哈希规范 | ## 典型用法 ### 重构 harness 重构可以改实现，不能改行为。这个判断交给引擎，不必通读 diff： 1. **重构前**：从当前代码抽出 BEFORE 模型（`uml_parse` 读已有的图，或按 schema 手写）。 2. **重构**。 3. **重构后**：抽出 AFTER 模型。 4. **回归**：`model_verify` 带 `beforeModel` 与 `stateMapping` 跑前后回归：行为是否保持、不变式是否连续、状态映射是否自洽。数据侧用 `model_datamodel_verify` 的 `beforeModel` / `fieldMapping` / `migrationMappings` 做同一件事的**数据版**。 5. **判定与留痕**：`report_diff` 拿基线报告比对。新增的 error 发现，就是这次重构不接受的理由。报告里的哈希让结论可复算。 它比较的是**你给的两份模型**，不是两份代码。每份模型是否忠实于对应代码，由第 1、3 步负责，它不代替你做。它也不读 diff、不改代码、不跑你的测试。它回答的是"行为还一样吗"，不是"重构得好不好"。 ### 代码流程审查 先把分支逻辑画成流程，再看这张图到底说了什么： 1. **抽流程**：把函数或服务里的分支写成 `LogicModelV1`，或者手画一张 `stateDiagram-v2` / PlantUML 图。 2. **读回模型**：手画的图交给 `uml_parse` 转成模型。读不动的行会变成警告，不会悄悄跳过。 3. **审查**：`uml_review` 报结构缺陷——不可达状态、死端、分支有歧义或没穷尽、自环没有出口、孤立节点、环——以及文档缺口。 4. **落回源码**：每条发现都回到代码核验。图画对了，不等于代码写对了。 它审的是你给的那张图和那份模型。图与代码是否一致，由第 1 步的抽取负责。 ### 状态机审查 把状态机建成可执行模型，让引擎去跑，而不是通读代码判断它会不会卡死： 1. **建模型**：手画的 `stateDiagram-v2` 或 PlantUML 状态图交给 `uml_parse`；也可以直接按 schema 写 `LogicModelV1`。 2. **跑检查**：`model_verify` 找的是不可达状态、吸收环、被静默忽略的事件、没有恢复路径的资源申请、预算超限，以及无法满足的时限。每一项都作为一个**带码**的发现报出，而码的前缀说明它属于哪一族。 3. **写清"永远/绝不"**：把这类断言写进 `invariants`，引擎会在全部可达状态上搜反例，并给出它找到的最短路径。 4. **落回源码**：报告里的 error 发现逐条回到代码。 并发断言分两半：**两个模型都碰同一个共享位置**这一类，由我们自己的 `model_compose_verify` 判（声明 `shared` 与 `accesses` 之后的 C3/C4/C5，包括丢更新）；源码级数据竞争、中断延迟、阻塞调用与漏掉的 `await` 仍路由到 TSan/Helgrind/CBMC/TLA+。硬实时语义（deadline、period）不在它的范围内。 ### 审计一张依赖图 组件图是关于「哪些模块可以依赖哪些」的断言。把它当图读，再问那些边是否被允许： 1. **给图**：PlantUML 的组件/包/类/部署图源码，或 Mermaid 类图。`uml_structure_verify` 把它解析成节点与边。 2. **说清什么被允许**（如果有规则）：一个含 `layers` 与 `rules` 的矩阵，每条规则点名一个 `source` 并给 `allow` / `deny` / `require`，再用 `default` 管其余。没有矩阵时，它只报结构缺陷。 3. **读发现**：孤立节点、从未声明过的端点、带最短路径的环、越过层的边、缺失的必需边，以及——一个节点都没声明时——**这份输入没有任何可审的东西**。 4. **换一种图就换个工具**：如果这张图是状态图或活动图，那是 `uml_review`，不是它。 它审的是**图**，不是代码。一张自洽的图仍可能画错了系统，所以要和源码侧扫描配对。手画的图报「标签漂移」时，`uml_explain_labels` 会打印该记号下解析器接受的标签写法。 ### 让设计对自己作出的声明负责 设计会对自己作出断言：这一层在那层之上、这个组件拥有那条依赖、这个接口比它的调用方窄。`model_design_review` 判定设计是否守住了这些承诺： 1. **把设计写成模型**：架构（节点与边），加上它声明的——分层、边界、允许与必需的边、带职责的类型、操作、转移、父类型。 2. **跑它**：`model_design_review` 报出设计与自相矛盾的地方，并**另外**报出它图的形状——环与打断环所需的最少边、承重元素、层级、扇入扇出。 3. **读那三个列表**：`violations` 决定判定；`signals` 值得一看但不使任何东西失败；`facts` 是**测量**，不是发现。`checksSkipped` 说明哪些原则因为**没声明任何可对照的东西**而没有检查。 **它从不按外部标准评判设计。** 它报的是：设计**与它自己声明的某件事**矛盾，或关于它的图的一个结构事实。问「这个设计好不好」是评审者的问题；这个工具回答的是另一个：**它就自己的说法而言，站得住吗**。 ### 两台必须互相配合的机器 一台机器**不会因为另一台**而死锁。当两个组件握手时，真正有意思的失败在**组合**里： 1. **各自建模**，然后一起给：`model_compose_verify` 收一个模型数组。 2. **点名共享事件**：如果一个握手只有在双方都就绪时才合法，把它写进 `rendezvous`。没写进去的事件只推进一台机器，所以等握手的机器可以先走任意多步自己的路。 3. **读 C1 与 C2**：一个可达节点上没有任何机器能前进、且有机器不是终止态（C1），以及一个**永远不会触发**的会合（C2）。两者都逐机给出理由，C1 还给最短反例。 模型里**没有速率比，也没有公平性约束**。单台机器自己的问题——不可达状态、不变式、成本对预算——用 `model_verify`。 ### 并发声明：挖掘并路由 「线程安全」「lock-free」「ISR 安全」都是需要某个能判定它们的工具的断言，而第一步是**把它们找出来**： 1. **扫文本**：`model_interleaving_scan` 收文档、计划或笔记，报出风险点——那条声明、共享状态、中断、临界区，以及异步的那些（`async`、`await`、`promise`、事件循环、回调）。每条发现都带 `family`（threads / synchronization / async / interrupts / shared-state），绝对式断言按 error 报。 2. **看每条绝对声明欠着什么**：「不可能有数据竞争」这类声明会被报为 error，要求**专门的**验证，且每条发现都点名能判定它的分析——竞争用 TSan 或 Helgrind，有界证明用 CBMC，协议用 TLA+，中断用 RTOS 感知的分析。 3. **去做那个分析**：本插件不运行它，也不对并发安全作任何证明。 它读的是**文本**。它看不见你的线程，而**一次干净的扫描不是健康证明**——它的含义是没找到声明，这是另一个命题。 ### 一次迁移：前后两份模型 迁移是两份模型，加一个「数据活下来了」的断言。把两份都给出去，这个断言就变成可核查的： 1. **两份模型**：改动前的 schema 与改动后的 schema，各自是含实体、字段、键与关系的数据模型。 2. **说清字段怎么走**：`fieldMapping` 从旧路径到新路径，加上 `migrationMappings`——用于来源不是它自己旧名字的字段。 3. **跑比对**：`model_datamodel_verify` 带 `beforeModel`，检查迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称，以及前后数据回归。 4. **读那条警告**：新 schema 里声明为 `required`、却没有任何东西供给它的字段，会报 `DS2_REQUIRED_FIELD_UNSOURCED`。它是 **warning**，所以判定停在 `pass_with_findings`——**这是一个要做的决定，不是引擎可以替你宣布的失败**。 它比较的是**你给的两份模型**。任一份是否忠实于它所描述的数据库，是抽取那一步的事，这个工具不做。 ### 图的导入与导出：设计冻结与长期迭代 这里存的是**源文件**，不是截图：`uml_render` 写出 Mermaid / PlantUML 源，`uml_parse` 把源读回模型。一份图因此能当两种东西用： - **设计冻结的留档**：把图源、模型和那一次的验证报告一起提交进仓库，作为某个时间点的设计记录。模型里可以放 `_` 前缀的元数据（单据号、日期、负责人、抽取时留下的保留意见），这些键不参与哈希，补档案信息不会改变结论的身份。 - **长期迭代的参考**：下一次改动时重新抽出模型、重跑验证，再用 `report_diff` 与冻结的那份报告比对。新增的 error 是这次改动引入的，消失的说明旧问题已经解决；哈希让"还是不是同一份模型"可判定，不必肉眼比图。 需要交给外部检查器时，同一份模型可以用 `model_export` 导出成 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN 的原生输入。 界线：它保存并比对的是**模型与图的源文件**，渲染出来的图片只是副产品。图变了模型没变、或模型变了图没变，都会在下一次解析或比对时暴露。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 做什么 | |---|---| | `uml_render` | 模型 → 图源（Mermaid / PlantUML），可指定图族。记号表达不了的视图会被拒绝，并说明理由 | | `uml_parse` | 图源 → 该图族的模型；不属于状态机/流程的族会按名拒绝，而不是硬当作状态机解析 | | `uml_review` | 审查建模：结构缺陷、文档缺口、render↔parse 往返一致性；给模型、给图，或两者对照 | | `uml_explain_labels` | 打印解析器接受的标签与注释契约，不需要图 | | `model_verify` | 状态机 / 协议的可执行验证（结构检查、对抗性探测、预算、时限、前后回归） | | `model_compose_verify` | 两台及以上机器的组合检查（死锁、永不发生的会合；声明了共享位置后还有无序写 C4 与非原子更新 C5） | | `model_datamodel_verify` | 数据模型与迁移验证 | | `model_interleaving_scan` | 并发 / 同步 / 异步声明的挖掘与路由 | | `model_export` | 导出到外部检查器（UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN） | | `uml_structure_verify` | 依赖图审计（含依赖矩阵与多层级细化） | | `model_design_review` | 设计审阅：依赖图形状 + 设计自身声明的契约（分层、职责边界、可替换性、接口宽度） | | `report_diff` | 两份报告比对：新增/消失/变化的发现 | ## 怎么读报告 工具的产出是一份报告，结论只在 `verdict` 里：**看 `verdict`，不看 `ok`**。`ok` 在各族的含义不同——多数族在评审失败时仍是 `true`，组合族在出现 error 级发现时是 `false`——所以它不能当判定读；把它当判定读，会得出与报告相反的结论。 | 字段 | 说明 | |---|---| | `verdict` | 判定：`pass`、`pass_with_findings`、`fail` | | `verdictReason` | 一句话说明为什么是这个判定 | | `hashes` | `hashSpec` 与 `modelHash`；前后回归另带 `beforeModelHash`、`afterModelHash`。同一份模型永远得到同一个哈希 | | `nextSteps` | 引擎建议的下一步 | | `schema` | 报告的版本化契约，例如 `model-everything/verify/v1`。要按字段分支，就分支在它上面 | | `truncated` | 搜索撞到上限就停了。**截断不等于通过**，是没结论；某个性质没判定出来时，报告里会出现 `_UNDECIDED` | 默认返回正文。要完整 JSON，传 `reportView: "full"`。 `ok` 为 `false` 时判定也是 `fail`，但含义不同：工具根本没跑。原因写在 `errorCode` 里——输入不合法、图族不支持，或声明的 `intent` 服务不了。这类拒绝的 `verdictReason` 以 `the tool did not run:` 开头。 报告怎么读，有一份成体系的说明：[`skills/model-everything-report-reading/`](skills/model-everything-report-reading/) 讲阅读顺序（先看跑没跑、再看判了什么、最后看该做什么）、发现分别放在哪一层、以及两处最容易读反的地方。结构由一个**从真实报告生成的思维导图**给出：[`docs/report-reading/mindmap.mmd`](docs/report-reading/mindmap.mmd)，`tests/report-reading` 会在图与引擎不一致时失败。 `uml_render`、`uml_parse`、`uml_review` 另收一个 `intent`，用来说明这份产物要做什么：给人看（`present`）、要被验证引擎读回（`verify`）、还是要证明渲染与模型一致（`fidelity`）。服务不了这个用途的视图会被直接拒绝，而不是勉强画出来。 ## 示例 `examples/` 里是可以直接跑的样本模型，配 [`examples/README.md`](examples/README.md) 说明各自的看点和预期结果。它们是文档，不是测试夹具——各测试套件读自己的 `tests/<套件>/fixtures/`： - `examples/order-state-machine.before.json` 与 `examples/order-state-machine.after.json`：订单流程的前后两份模型，用来跑前后回归。 - `examples/control-dispatcher.json`：带预算与锁配对的分发状态机，预期零错误。 - `examples/control-dispatcher.overbudget.json`：同一个机器换上更慢的看门狗处理，预期报出一条 `A12_BUDGET_OVER`，并给出最短的超预算路径。 - `examples/ecommerce-data-model.json`，以及 `examples/user-migration.before.json` 与 `examples/user

plugins.description: A desktop pet that shows what your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness) are doing — and lets you answer their permission prompts
plugins.readme_text:
# agent-pet

A floating desktop pet for coding agents. One character per active agent (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, or anything that can run a shell command); her mood follows the agent, and when an agent asks for permission the pet shows the prompt in a bubble you can answer without switching windows.

![agent-pet showing a permission bubble](docs/screenshot.png)

Pets appear only while a session is working, waiting for you, or just finished. Everything is local: agents append JSON lines to a file and the overlay tails it. Nothing is sent over the network and there are no accounts; the optional DSH plugin opens a loopback-only port (127.0.0.1) for the overlay's open-session commands.

## Requirements

- macOS 14 or later
- Swift 6 toolchain (Xcode or the Command Line Tools)
- Python 3 (ships with macOS; used by the installer)

ChatGPT (the chat app) has no local plugin API, so there is no integration with it. Codex running inside ChatGPT.app is covered by the Codex plugin below.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rpegorov/agent-pet.git
cd agent-pet
scripts/install.sh                  # build, install to ~/.local/agent-pet, hook up Claude Code and Codex
scripts/install.sh --launch-agent   # also start the overlay at login
```

`install.sh` also accepts `--no-claude-hooks` and `--no-codex-hooks` (use these with the plugins below), and `--uninstall`.

## Connect your agents

Use **either** the plugin **or** the `install.sh` hooks for a given agent, not both. Both together would deliver every event twice and ask every permission twice; the emitter does not de-duplicate because it cannot tell which hook fired first. Plugins carry only the hook wiring, so run `scripts/install.sh --no-claude-hooks --no-codex-hooks` once for the binary and the overlay.

**Claude Code.** `install.sh` adds hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json`. Or, as a plugin:

```
/plugin marketplace add rpegorov/agent-pet
/plugin install agent-pet@agent-pet
```

**Codex.** `install.sh` adds hooks to `~/.codex/hooks.json` and trusts them in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Or, as a plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add rpegorov/agent-pet
codex plugin add codex-agent-pet@agent-pet
```

Codex does not trust the plugin's hooks on a command-line install, so they stay silent until you approve them (see Troubleshooting). The `install.sh` route has no such step.

**DeepSeek Harness (DSH).** `plugins/dsh-agent-pet` is a standalone DSH plugin. In your profile's `package.json` add a dependency `"dsh-agent-pet": "link:/path/to/agent-pet/plugins/dsh-agent-pet"` and add `"dsh-agent-pet"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, install, and restart DSH. It reports session state and lets the overlay open a session or start a chat in the Harness UI.

**Anything else** (scripts, task runners, other agents):

```sh
agent-pet-emit send --agent glm --session task-1 --label "refactor" --mood working
agent-pet-emit send --agent glm --session task-1 --mood complete
```

## Event protocol

`agent-pet-emit` appends one line per event to `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` (override with `AGENT_PET_LOG`); the overlay tails the file. The file is rotated to `events.jsonl.1` above 512 KiB.

```json
{"v":1,"agent":"claude","session":"5e9d","mood":"working","label":"Bash","ts":1792276251.42}
```

`mood` is `idle`, `working`, `attention`, `complete` or `ended` (removes the session). `label` is at most 40 characters. Optional fields, omitted when unknown: `cwd`, `app` (bundle id of the hosting app), `tty`, `detail` (permission summary, at most 200 characters), `permission` (id of a pending request).

Decay: working with no event for 120 s is hidden, complete is hidden after 10 s, attention after 10 min, a session silent for 30 min is dropped. An agent's pet shows the highest-priority mood of its live sessions: attention, working, complete.

## Permission bubble

With the overlay running, `agent-pet-emit permit` (the PermissionRequest hook) shows the pending tool call in a bubble with **Deny**, **In agent** and **Allow**, and a countdown.

- The bubble shows the whole tool input (pretty-printed JSON, capped at 8 KiB). If the input is capped or unreadable, Allow is withheld.
- **In agent** hands the prompt back to the agent's own dialog. If nobody answers before the countdown ends (at most 40 s, `AGENT_PET_PERMIT_WAIT` seconds, default 30), or the overlay stops running, the native dialog appears as usual. The pet never auto-allows.
- Tools that ask you something (`AskUserQuestion`, `ExitPlanMode`) are never turned into a bubble.
- Requests live in `~/.agent-pet/permissions/` (owner-only) and are removed when answered, expired or when the hook is killed.
- The overlay's own texts (Deny, In agent, Allow, status labels) are English and not localised; labels that come from agents (tool names, session titles) appear as sent.
- To turn the bubble off, quit the overlay (the hook then stays silent), or change the `PermissionRequest` command from `permit` to `hook` in the agent's hook config.

## Privacy

agent-pet keeps everything on your Mac and sends nothing over the network.

- **What is written.** `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` holds one line per hook event: agent name, session id, mood, a short label (tool name, session title or notification text), the working directory, the hosting app's bundle id, the terminal tty and, for permission requests, a summary of the tool call (at most 200 characters). Prompts, tool output and file contents are not recorded.
- **Permission requests.** While a request is pending, `~/.agent-pet/permissions/` holds its full tool input (at most 8 KiB). The file is deleted when the request is answered, expires or the hook is killed; leftovers older than 2 minutes are cleaned up.
- **Access.** The directory is owner-only (0700) and the log is 0600. The log is rotated at 512 KiB, keeping one previous file.
- **What is read.** The overlay reads the event log, and, to open a Claude Desktop session, the session index in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code-sessions` (read only). Selecting a Terminal or iTerm2 tab uses AppleScript and asks macOS for Automation permission once.
- **System log.** Clicks and jumps are logged under the subsystem `agent-pet` with agent, session id, app and the opened URL; no tool input or paths.
- **Network.** None outbound. The DSH plugin listens on a loopback-only port and accepts commands only from local processes and the Harness web UI; the overlay talks to it over `127.0.0.1`.

Delete `~/.agent-pet` to remove all recorded data.

## Uninstall

```sh
scripts/install.sh --uninstall
```

Removes the binaries, hooks, trust entries and LaunchAgent. A no-op `agent-pet-emit` stub stays behind so sessions that are still open do not report a missing command; restart them and delete the stub. Plugins are removed with `/plugin uninstall`, `codex plugin remove` or by editing the DSH profile.

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing appears.** Is the overlay running (`pgrep -x AgentPet`)? Does `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` grow when an agent works? If not, the hooks are not installed or the agent was started before they were; restart the agent.
- **Codex plugin hooks do nothing.** Codex 0.163 does not trust hooks from a plugin installed with `codex plugin add`; they ran only with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. Approve them in Codex (`/hooks`) or use `scripts/install.sh`, which writes the trust entries itself. Re-run `install.sh` after changing a hook command: the trust is tied to its text.
- **DSH changes are not picked up.** DSH caches plugin ES modules; restart it after installing or editing a plugin.
- **DSH commands are refused.** The plugin's bridge answers only the Harness web UI origin (`http://127.0.0.1:50306`) and local processes; a UI served from another origin cannot read its queue.

## License

MIT. The sprite art in `Sources/AgentPet/Resources` is included under the same license.

plugins.description: DSH (DeepSeek Harness) plugin: configured extra writable roots for the fs tools and the sandboxed shell — first-try writes with no approval, plus a Web settings page and structure-anchored path patterns.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-extra-paths

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Let DSH **write to a set of configured external paths on the first try, with no approval**: this covers the `write`/`edit`
tools and `bash` subprocesses alike. The plugin works by wrapping services (it does not change DSH core) and ships a Web
settings page plus a preview of the effective roots for the current workspace.

## Install

Requires DSH `0.1.5` / `0.2.0` / `0.2.1` (outside that range the install gate refuses the package).

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-extra-paths            # <name> = your profile
```

From a checkout instead of the registry:

```bash
pnpm install && pnpm build
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-extra-paths   # path = absolute path to this repo
```

Then open the **Extra paths** card under **Settings → Plugins**, or **Extra writable paths** in the settings sidebar.

## Configuration

Write it into the `extra-paths` section of the settings document `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`, or just use the settings page
(**saving takes effect immediately, no restart needed**). `<work root>` below is a placeholder for the directory that
holds your projects (an absolute path, or one starting with `~/`) — replace it with a path of your own:

```yaml
extra-paths:
  paths:
    - <work root>/notes/home                   # default scope/surfaces
    - path: ../../notes/home                   # relative paths resolve against the session workspace
      scope: always-write
    - path: <work root>/some-repo
      scope: write
      surfaces: [fs]                           # only the write/edit tools may write here
```

| scope | session `read-only` | session `workspace-write` |
|---|---|---|
| `write` (default) | denied | writable |
| `always-write` | writable | writable |

`surfaces`: `fs` = the `write`/`edit`/str-replace tools; `shell` = `bash` subprocesses. Reads and execution are not
sandboxed to begin with.

### How relative paths resolve

Relative paths resolve against **each session's own workspace** (the settings page has a "base workspace" field so you
can preview this):

| Spelling | Resolves to | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `..` | `<work root>` | the **parent** of the workspace; that directory and all of its siblings become writable |
| `../some-repo` | `<work root>/some-repo` | grants exactly one sibling repository (more precise than `..`, recommended) |
| `../../notes/home` | `<work root>/notes/home` | go up a few levels and into another tree |
| `~/notes/home` | under your home | independent of the workspace; `~user` is not expanded (same as the host) |

### Patterns: anchor a grant to directory structure (no hard-coded paths)

A `path` can use wildcards to describe **a group of directories**, turning "a certain directory exists somewhere in this
path" into a condition:

| Spelling | Matches (the granted root) |
|---|---|
| `<work root>/**/.worktrees/..` | every **repository root that contains `.worktrees`** (the parent of `.worktrees`) |
| `<work root>/**/.worktrees/*` | each individual worktree (`.git` and the main checkout are never touched) |
| `<work root>/<some-repo>/.worktrees/*` | every worktree of one repository (**zero traversal cost**, recommended) |
| `<work root>/*/notes` | the `notes` directory under every repository/project |

Syntax: `*` = exactly one level, `**` = at most 3 levels (**only directories that actually exist** match, so
"`.worktrees` must exist" comes for free); a trailing `..` moves up **after** matching (so `…/.worktrees/..` is "the
parent of `.worktrees`", rather than something lexical collapsing eats away).

Safety bounds (hard constraints, not advice):

- the wildcard needs a **literal anchor** before it, at least two segments long, absolute or starting with `~/` —
  `/**`, `~/**`, `/srv/**` are refused outright
- traversal **never enters** `node_modules` or `.git`, and `**` never enters hidden directories (`.worktrees` is a
  literal, so it still matches at its own level)
- bounded: `**` covers at most 3 levels, and more than 4096 directories or more than 256 matches makes **the whole
  pattern inert** (fail closed — never a partial, unpredictable grant); the reason is reported as a warning
- expansions are cached for 30 seconds, so a **newly created worktree is picked up within 30 seconds**

The settings page shows the **resolved absolute path** live for every row (symlinks follow the host's canonical
preview) and, for a pattern row, the match count as `[active ×N]` plus each concrete root below it; zero matches and
blocked patterns are both spelled out — so there is no need to "save first and then check whether it resolved".

## Known limits

- Per-path "no restrictions at all" is not achievable: the bash sandbox works at whole-invocation granularity.
- Relative paths resolve against the session workspace, so the same entry points at different directories in different
  workspaces — the settings page preview shows the actual resolution.
- The shell side is not widened on Windows; `always-write` weakens what the `read-only` stop button can do for that path.
- Files written outside the workspace do not appear in the `deliverables` workspace-changes card.

plugins.description: Android companion for DeepSeek Harness | chat, goals, approvals & notifications from your phone, over your LAN. Kotlin + Jetpack Compose.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. The [**wiki**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki) is the user-facing guide: [getting started](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Getting-Started), [connecting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Connecting), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Troubleshooting), a [feature tour](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Feature-Tour) and an [FAQ](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/FAQ). --- ## Screenshots | Connect | Chat | Trajectory | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | | | | | Recent harnesses with live reachability, LAN discovery, manual `host:port`, auto-connect. | Streamed turns, a glyph per tool, expandable tool cards, permission picker. | The same session as a per-turn ledger with usage totals. | | Session details | Subagents | |:--:|:--:| | | | | Context breakdown, goal, plan mode, background jobs, queued turns, host info, session-log export. | The subagent catalog — open a child's transcript, follow up, or interrupt it. | ## Features - Connecting — finds a harness on your Wi-Fi with an active subnet scan and a readiness handshake, remembers hosts and probes them for liveness on the way in, takes a manual `host:port`, handles loopback for same-device setups, and auto-connects when you tell it to (last used, LAN, or same device). - Navigation — the drawers work like Discord's: swipe right from the left edge for the workspace-grouped chat list, swipe left to close it, swipe left from the right edge for the session details panel. - Chat — streamed turns with reasoning disclosure, markdown, terminal/diff/read/search/web tool cards, a queue dock where you can edit, remove or steer a queued turn, history paging, and multi-photo and file attachments. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. The automatic check also runs again when you come back to the app after a few hours. - Workspace links in replies drawn as file and folder pills; a folder opens in Files. - A redesigned Details panel, Workspace screen and Settings, with archived sessions on a tab of their own. ### Added in 0.14.0 - A `/` menu above the composer with the session's commands and skills. - A picker for the dsh-rewind plugin's `/rewind` and `/undo` that asks for confirmation before it restores files. The transcript hides what a rewind withdrew and marks the cut. ### Added in 0.13.0 - Automation catalog, timing edits, delivery history and session shortcuts. - Plugin installation, updates, toggles, removal, progress and recovery. Create plugin stages an unsent draft with the Creator preset when the host offers it. - Timed questions, continued replies, saved answer drafts and reopenable plans. - Draft text and file, folder and session references saved across app restarts. - Model search, YAML document properties and multiline goal editing. - Reverse-proxy path support and tool argument previews while the model is writing. ## Requirements - Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26). - A running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) at `0.2.1-alpha.2`, the protocol baseline for DSH Mobile `0.16.0`. Existing protocol fallbacks remain for `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.x` and `0.1.6-alpha.x`; new management features need host support. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [0.13.0 validation status](docs/VALIDATION-0.13.0.md) for what has been checked on this baseline. ## Quick start 1. Install the latest APK from [Releases](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/releases/latest). 2. Open the app and choose how to connect. Relay and local network are two different setups, not two settings of one, so pick the one that matches wha

plugins.description: DSH plugin: convert a request into MiL with Sarashina, review it, then hand it to the model dsh is running (TUI and Web UI)
plugins.readme_text:
# 1tempo

曖昧な依頼文を MiL へ変換し、承認してから dsh で選択中のモデルへ渡す dsh プラグイン。

```
/onetempo 3Dモデルを作って
  ↓ sarashina が MiL へ変換（mil-spec を system に渡す）
  ↓ 原文と MiL を表示し、承認（必要なら修正）
  ↓ 承認済みの MiL を、dsh で選択中のモデルへ渡す
```

- 確定設計: [architecture.md](architecture.md)
- dsh への要望（会話へ書く API）: [dsh-feature-request.md](dsh-feature-request.md)
- 企画の原案・質疑応答・実測レポート（`proposal.md` / `qa-record.md` / `preflight-report-*.md`）はローカル記録のため、この公開リポジトリには含めていない。本文中の `preflight-report-run*.md` はその記録のファイル名を示す。

## 何をするか

1. `/onetempo` が起動したときだけ動く。通常の依頼文には反応しない。
2. 依頼文を [Sarashina API](https://docs.sarashina.ai/) に送り、MiL へ変換する。
3. 原文と MiL を表示し、承認を求める。承認前に編集もできる。
4. 承認された MiL を、dsh の選択モデルへ **利用者のメッセージとして** 渡す（`source.kind: 'user'`）。dsh は `source.kind === 'user'` のメッセージだけを利用者の行として扱い、`/rewind` の戻り先にもする（それ以外はコンテキスト行になり、会話に出ない）。変換の来歴はプラグインの storage ログと通知に残す。
5. 原文・MiL・逆翻訳・変換モデル・呼び出し回数・承認有無を dsh の storage に記録する。storage が使えない場合は「ログ: 保存できませんでした（理由）」と出し、**保存したように見せない**（セッション内の記録だけを保持する）。

## 必要なもの

- dsh（`@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui` が入ったプロファイル）
- Node.js 24 以降（テストと測定ツールで確認）
- `SARASHINA_API_KEY`（[Sarashina](https://sarashina.ai) で発行。無償ベータ、Google ログイン、事前申し込み不要）

キーの指定方法は以下のいずれか（優先順位順）:
1. `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`（dsh 標準の認証情報ファイル、推奨）
2. 環境変数 `SARASHINA_API_KEY`（`.env` を使う場合は `node --env-file=.env`）

```powershell
# 測定ツールの例（~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml にキーがあれば --env-file 不要）
node tools/preflight-decode.mjs --dry
```

## 使い方

```
/onetempo [mini|nano] [back] <依頼文>
```

| 引数 | 意味 |
| --- | --- |
| `mini` / `nano` | 変換モデルの上書き。`sarashina3-mini`（6 RPM） / `sarashina3-nano`（60 RPM、既定） |
| `back` | 逆翻訳（MiL を自然語へ戻したもの）も表示する。省略時は設定の既定 |
| `<依頼文>` | 変換対象。フラグの後に来た文字列をそのまま使う |

引数なしの `/onetempo` は使い方を表示する。

> **名前について**: プロジェクト名は 1tempo だが、コマンドと識別子は `onetempo`。dsh のコマンド名とプラグイン所有の設定名前空間は `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/`（英小文字で始まる）に一致する必要があり、当初案の `1tempo` は数字始まりのため拒否される（実測: `command name "1tempo" must match ...` / `invalid TUI settings-section namespace: 1tempo`）。表示名（`1tempo`、設定セクションの見出し、`source.plugin`）は `1tempo` のまま。

### 表示と承認

- 変換結果は **通知欄** に出る。**200 セル以内に収まる形に整形する**（`1tempo: 送信しました…` / `MiL: <送信する MiL>` / 逆翻訳・ログ行）。
  - dsh はプラグインのコマンド結果を `channel.notify(cleanRenderText(text, COMMAND_RESULT_CELLS = 200))` で通知欄に描く。200 セルを超えた分は `…` で切られるため、先頭を MiL にし、続く注記は予算内の分だけ載せる（プラグイン側では切り詰めない）
  - 長い MiL の全文は承認ダイアログの初期値（490 セルまで）で読める
- **会話に出るのは送信メッセージの本文だけ**（`content`）。本文は **MiL のみ**。
  - `content` は「会話に表示されるテキスト」と「モデルが読むテキスト」を兼ねる。dsh に両者を分ける欄は無い（実測: `tools/inspect-session-log.mjs --grep` で `agent/inbox/spliced` に本文が入ることを確認）。そのため原文を会話に出すと、そのままモデルにも渡る
  - `includeOriginalInMessage: true` にすると本文が「依頼: <原文>」→「MiL: …」になる。会話の行が自分の言葉で始まり `/rewind` で識別しやすいが、**MiL の圧縮効果は失われる**。既定は `false`
